messages.author: Muhammad Sameer India
messages.content:
I'm Sameer, a 2nd-year CS student and builder from India (IST). I'm super excited to be participating in the Meta AI Global Hackathon!

I'm in the Indie Developer track, and I'm building RealityLab — an AI tool that scans real-world objects (like a toy car) and turns them into interactive, exploded-view engineering blueprints, complete with a "Build Mode" to recreate them.

I'm especially interested in multimodal AI and how it can make engineering accessible to everyone. For this project, I'm building a FastAPI backend and React frontend, powered by Meta's SAM 3.1, Muse Spark, and Muse Image.

Looking forward to learning from everyone, sharing ideas, and seeing what you all build! Good luck, everyone! 🚀

messages.author: shashCodes
messages.content:
Hello Everbody, I’m Shashwat, a final-year B.Tech IT student from Pune. I also run a YouTube channel with ~8.9k subscribers, where I help students with CET prep.

About me, I’ve built:
• PrepPilot, a full-stack platform for CET prep that I made for my channel’s students (Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, Redis, JWT, Docker): https://cet-sheet.tech
• NyayaSetu, a legal-assistant project I led with a team of 5, using hybrid RAG retrieval (BM25 + TF-IDF) with a locally run LLM (Phi-3 via Ollama)
• 300+ DSA and 80+ SQL problems solved on LeetCode

Portfolio: https://shashwatsportfolio-six.vercel.app/

I’m comfortable taking an idea from zero to a deployed prototype: backend, database, auth, Docker, and an LLM/RAG layer on top. I’ve led a team of 5, run a project with real student users, and I’m good at presenting and GD, so I can handle the pitch/demo too. I am so excited for collaborating with curious minds, lets build something crazy together..

messages.content:
Hi everyone! 👋 I’m **Maftuh Ichsan** from Indonesia.

I’m a full-stack developer and startup builder, and I’m currently building **Kirimin ID**, a business technology platform that brings together several digital tools and services for businesses.

My background is mainly in full-stack development, API integrations, backend systems, automation, SaaS products, and cloud infrastructure. I usually work with technologies such as Laravel, Node.js/TypeScript, React/Next.js, MySQL/PostgreSQL, Docker, and various third-party APIs.

For this hackathon, I’m planning to explore how **Meta’s AI models and APIs** can be integrated into Kirimin ID to create new AI-powered capabilities for real business workflows. I’ll be focusing on practical AI, automation, multimodal use cases, and agentic experiences while keeping the project closely connected to a real startup environment.

I’m joining the **Startup Track** and I’m excited to experiment with Meta’s latest AI technology, learn from the community, and see what everyone builds.

Nice to meet you all

Hey! I’m Shashwat, a final-year B.Tech IT student from Pune. I also run a YouTube channel with ~8.9k subscribers, where I help students with MHTCET/JEE prep. 
www.linkedin.com/in/shashwatdiwan
About me, I’ve built:
• PrepPilot, a full-stack platform for CET prep that I made for my channel’s students (Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, Redis, JWT, Docker): https://cet-sheet.tech
• NyayaSetu, a legal-assistant project I led with a team of 5, using hybrid RAG retrieval (BM25 + TF-IDF) with a locally run LLM (Phi-3 via Ollama)
• 300+ DSA and 80+ SQL problems solved on LeetCode

Portfolio: https://shashwatsportfolio-six.vercel.app/

I’m looking for 2–3 people who are strong in [frontend/UI, ML/fine-tuning, or product/pitching]. If you like shipping fast and want to build something that works end to end, DM me.

I’m comfortable taking an idea from zero to a deployed prototype: backend, database, auth, Docker, and an LLM/RAG layer on top. I’ve led a team of 5, run a project with real student users, and I’m good at presenting and GD, so I can handle the pitch/demo too.

messages.author: WAYNE LEVI
messages.content:
More like Jarvis than a chatbot.

A chatbot: you type a question, it types an answer back. That's it.

Vee Vee: you talk to her out loud and she talks back — like Jarvis. But she goes one step past Jarvis: she's got a gut reaction first, her own flow, and a conscience, and she can speak up on her own instead of only answering when asked. She remembers you and checks in on you, too.

Chatbot waits for questions. Vee Vee's a companion.

messages.content:
Hi all! I’m Shivani 👋 . I mostly work in Python on developer tooling and distributed systems (consensus, storage, ML infra).

Building: codelore, which captures the knowledge that only lives in senior engineers’ heads.

“Why is this here?” Hover any line in VS Code and Muse Spark tells you its story from git history and PR discussions, citing every commit and PR.
Codebase heat map of risky files and bus factor (“only Rahul knows this file”).
Blameless postmortem writer. It turns the incident Slack thread, logs and call recording (Muse Voice Transcribe) into a postmortem draft. Anything without evidence behind it gets flagged instead of made up.

Track: Build for Your World. Every team I’ve worked on lost days to “who knows why this exists?” and to writing postmortems.

[Solo / Open to 1–2 teammates, especially frontend or VS Code extension folks.] Happy to chat dev tools anytime!

Hey everyone! 

I’m Aghede David based in Abuja Nigeria. I'm a Security Engineer and SOC analyst. I build secure, scalable systems and exploring how AI can solve real-world problems.

I bring experience with Python, Go, PostgreSQL, Docker, gRPC, and security engineering. I’ve been working on projects involving context-aware continuous authentication and AI agent access control.

For this hackathon, I plan on building an Agent Action Firewall a Go-based security proxy that sits between AI agents and their tools, evaluates tool calls against policies and contextual risk, and blocks unauthorized or potentially malicious actions. I also want to implement tamper-evident, hash-chained audit logs and demonstrate the firewall stopping a prompt-injection attack that attempts to exfiltrate a sensitive file.

Hi everyone! I'm Alberto — an industrial engineer based in Florida, working the night shift in warehouse distribution operations. I build for the problems I live every shift.

I'm solo in the Indie track (Build for Your World), building an operations copilot for shift leads: a deterministic engine computes the shift plan, mid-shift pace alerts and staff reassignments, and Meta's models explain those alerts and answer "what if…?" questions by calling the engine as a tool. The model never makes up a number — every figure comes from the engine.

I'm solo in the Indie track (Build for Your World), building an operations copilot for shift leads: a deterministic engine computes the shift plan, mid-shift pace alerts and staff reassignments, and Meta's models explain those alerts and answer "what if…?" questions by calling the engine as a tool. The model never makes up a number — every figure comes from the engine.

Hi everyone! I'm Carlos González, a Software Engineer at IAMIA, based in Cancún, Mexico.

I build AI agents and automations, and I write most of my code by directing agents with TDD and ODD: first I define what gets built and how to tell it's done right, then the agent writes the code. My day-to-day stack is Node.js, NestJS, React and Next.js, and on the side I play around with Unity, Blender, Hyperframes and Palmier Pro.

I studied Business Administration at Université Paris-Saclay and Computer Science in Quebec, so I speak Spanish, French and English.

messages.author: Timur Salakhetdinov
messages.content:
Hi all 👋 I'm Timur from Hamburg.

I'm a Working Student in Analytics at InnoGames with 10 years in analytics across telecom, finance, insurance and gaming, and I'm finishing an M.Sc. in Management & Data Science at Leuphana University (March 2027).

At InnoGames I work on game analytics: engagement and monetisation dashboards for our game teams, funnel and A/B analyses, and I'm prototyping a financial model in Microsoft Fabric. I also built a TabPFN pipeline for net revenue forecasting, which grew into my thesis on foundation models plus LLM-compiled text covariates.

Here I'm building a multi-agent system that helps games improve the new-player experience, using Meta's multimodal models.

Happy to swap notes on agent evals, game analytics or forecasting.
 Portfolio: https://timursalakhetdinov.com LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/timursalakhetdinov GitHub: https://github.com/TimurSalakhetdinov

Hi all, I'm Tilak from Kathmandu, Nepal. AI/ML engineer (production multi-agent systems on AWS) and researcher on evaluation reliability: when can you trust a model's judgment?

Indie track: building Argus, an agentic video editor. Give it raw footage and a plain instruction like "make a 30-second vertical reel of every time someone laughs": Muse Spark plans and calls tools, SAM 3.1 segments and tracks what you name, Muse Voice Transcribe handles the audio, and Argus renders the cut with the reason for each moment.

Happy to talk agents, video understanding or evals.
https://github.com/parajulitilak · https://www.linkedin.com/in/parajulitilak

messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋 I'm Yatharth, joining solo from Singapore 🇸🇬

My journey started at ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation), where I worked as a Scientist/Engineer on satellite imagery, SAR, and Earth observation. I later moved into research engineering at NUS, working on FPGA-based computing and hardware acceleration.

I'm currently a Senior Research Engineer at Singapore Management University (SMU), where I work on legal AI research infrastructure, data provenance, and building reliable systems that turn complex research into usable tools.

I've always been fascinated by the intersection of AI, space technology, scientific research, and systems engineering.

Would love to connect with people working on AI agents, multimodal systems, open-weight models, inference engineering, or scientific AI. Also keen to exchange ideas and learn from what everyone is building.

🔗 LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/yatharthsant

💻 GitHub: https://github.com/ysant77

Good luck, everyone! Looking forward to seeing some incredible builds here.

messages.author: mello
messages.content:
Hey — Abderrahmene, from Oran, Algeria.

I build the software Algerian merchants sell with: a cash-on-delivery order stack,
a multi-store platform and a Shopify app, live across hundreds of storefronts.

Here ~95% of online orders are paid in cash at the door, and the sale doesn't close
on a product page — it closes in Instagram comments and Messenger DMs, in Algerian
darija, often by voice note.

I'm building the whole loop: one product photo and a prompt become the ad creative,
the campaign is created on Facebook and Instagram through the Marketing API, and
the agent then handles the conversation it generates — it answers the customer,
prices the delivery for their own commune, and creates the order. The delivery
outcome goes back as the real signal.

What I can help with: Meta Marketing API, cash-on-delivery logistics (35+ carriers),
and Arabic typography in generated images — image models deform Arabic script, so I
compose it as a deterministic SVG layer.

Solo, Indie track. Happy to talk to anyone working on agents, Arabic/RTL, or
emerging-market commerce.

messages.author: KuaV
messages.content:
Hi everyone, my name is Harris an AI student from University of Technology Malaysia

Im interested in building a Proof-of-Done, a verification layer for computer use agents. Research shows the top failure of these agents is "false success": saying "done" when the screen says otherwise. My agent has to prove every action with before/after evidence (Muse Spark + SAM 3.1), or it retries/asks instead of claiming success.

I care a lot about honest evaluation (hidden test sets, publishing failures) and AI cognitive architectures.

Happy to chat about GUI grounding, agent verification, voice UX or evals  and always open to feedback! 
GitHub: https://github.com/
Linkedin:  (https://www.linkedin.com/in/harrisdanielhadnan/)

messages.author: Anuj Singh
messages.content:
👋 Hi everyone! I'm Anuj Singh from India, founder of NirmanOS (Startup track, solo).

🧱 Who I am: I run a brick kiln. I'm not a programmer by background; I build with AI coding tools and know the problem first-hand.

🛠️ What I bring: two WhatsApp agents already in real use:
• Bhatta Munshi: reads the kiln's handwritten Hindi diary from a photo and keeps the books
• JCB Hours Agent: reads hour-meter photos from machine operators and bills the kiln

🤝 What I'm building: "Bhatta Agents: two ledgers, one truth". The JCB owner's agent and the kiln's agent exchange signed bills agent-to-agent. Muse Spark acts as the owner's private auditor: it checks both books and explains any difference in plain Hindi. Nothing changes without the owner's yes.

Happy to chat with anyone building for small businesses, WhatsApp agents, Hindi/Indian languages, or agent-to-agent protocols. Good luck all! 🚀

Hey everyone! 👋

I'm Yehonatan from israel. I've been learning, building, and working as a developer for the past 20 years.

For this hackathon, I'm building an LashoHaraProtector — a real-time AI safety layer that monitors digital text inputs, flags potential Lashon Hara (harmful speech/gossip) using structured AI checks, and offers zero-delay rephrasing suggestions."

Key Features:

Real-time Detection: Identifies derogatory speech, unconstructive criticism, and gossip patterns.

Constructive Rephrasing: Context-aware rewrites that preserve the core message while removing harmful nuances.

Customizable Sensitivity: Allows users to set privacy filters and tone strictness based on the target audience (e.g., family group chats vs. work Slack).! 🚀

good luck to all!

Portfolio - https://portfolio.ysho.uk/

messages.content:
Hey everyone! I'm Lori, an Archaeological Anthropology senior at the University of Oregon, solo developer, and apparently someone who thinks a global AI hackathon is a perfectly reasonable place to jump into the deep end. 😂

I'm a bit of an oddball in the developer world. My background is in studying humans, institutions, power, and the stories we tell ourselves about how the world works. Somewhere along the way, I realized that AI could help us ask questions we haven't even thought to ask.

So I'm building Blindspot Engine, an AI research tool designed to find connections, contradictions, and missing pieces buried across mountains of evidence. But here's the twist: it doesn't just hunt for patterns. It tries to prove itself wrong.

I'm especially interested in what happens when we stop asking AI to give us answers and start asking it to challenge what we think we know.

I'm competing solo, learning as I go, and operating on the philosophy that if you want to fly, you have to jump.

So here I am. Jumping. 🚀

Can't wait to see what everyone creates, meet some brilliant weirdos, and find out just how far we can push this technology.

messages.author: Billydavis
messages.content:
Hey everyone! My name is Billy Davis from Hudson, North Carolina.
By day, I work full time in manufacturing as a machine operator and batch maker. Outside of work, I'm an independent AI/ML researcher and the founder of Hudson Forge Technologies, a small research operation I've been building out of my home lab.
My background isn't traditional. No university degree, no professional engineering team, just determination, a strong work ethic, and five kids who motivate me to keep pushing.
Over the past several months, I've studied AI, machine learning, deep learning, LLMOps/MLOps, cybersecurity, quantum computing, and software engineering through DeepLearning.AI, NVIDIA, IBM, and Duke University's LLMOps program, and I've put that learning to work in several independent projects, including IRMB (multi-model AI research), quantum computing on real IBM hardware, Sentinel (red-team testing of my own systems), and RIP (governed research pipelines).
I work solo, but I use multiple AI models as a collaborative research and engineering council.
For this hackathon, I'm building a portable agentic business protection system for small businesses: a lightweight security layer that runs on API or local models, evaluates threats with multiple models, and produces governed decisions with an auditable verdict ledger. The goal is to show not just detection, but reasoning about evidence, authorization boundaries, and appropriate action.
Long term, I want to turn this research into a real business that helps smaller organizations access security capabilities they otherwise couldn't afford.
Looking forward to learning from everyone and exchanging ideas. Good luck to everyone participating!

messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋🇬🇭

I'm **Collins Amoah**, a Software Developer, Graphic Designer, Tech Entrepreneur, and Founder & CEO of **FlockGuard AI**, joining from Accra, Ghana.

I've always been fascinated by one question: **How can technology solve problems that genuinely affect people's lives?**

My journey started with graphic design, bringing creative ideas to life. Somewhere along the way, I fell in love with software engineering. I realized I didn't just want to design how technology looks. **I wanted to build how it works.** 😂

Today, I work with JavaScript, React, Node.js, Express, Python, FastAPI, Firebase, MongoDB, and AI tools, while expanding my skills in TypeScript, Next.js, React Native, machine learning, system design, and AI agents.

But here's where things get interesting! 🚀

I'm building **FlockGuard AI**, an AI-powered poultry early-warning platform that helps farmers identify potential risks before they become serious.

Imagine a farmer losing valuable birds because small changes in feeding, water consumption, or behaviour went unnoticed. **What if AI could help detect those warning signs earlier?**

That's the problem we're working to solve.

Now I'm here, joining brilliant minds from around the world to explore AI agents, multimodal AI, and intelligent automation.

Am I excited? Absolutely. Ready to challenge myself? Definitely! 😂

I believe great technology isn't just about impressive code. **It's about solving meaningful problems and creating real-world impact.**

I'm here to learn, collaborate, exchange ideas, and push my limits.

Can't wait to meet everyone and see what you're building!

**Let's build something the world actually needs! 🌍🚀🔥**

messages.author: itsjerryinnit
messages.content:
Hey everyone, I’m Jerry, a solo founder from Nairobi, Kenya, and apparently someone who thinks a global AI hackathon is a perfectly reasonable place to try to teach AI to speak like us. 😂
I’m a bit of an oddball in the developer world too. I don’t come from AI research but from building tools for creators who post every day and still don’t see themselves in what AI writes for them. Somewhere along the way, I realised the problem wasn’t that creators needed more captions. It was that the captions didn’t sound like them.
So I’m building Yoyzie Voice, a caption assistant inside Yoyzie AI that learns a creator’s voice from their own past posts. It looks at the image, then generates captions in that voice in English, Swahili(our local language), and Sheng (the local slang) code-switching included, instead of flattening everyone into the same generic English.
I’m especially interested in what happens when we stop asking AI to write for people, and start asking it to preserve how people actually talk.
I’m competing on the Startup track, Build for Your World, learning as I go and operating on the philosophy that if AI doesn’t speak us, it doesn’t really serve us.
Can’t wait to see what everyone creates, meet some brilliant minds and swap feedback and test each other’s demos.   My portfolio: https://jerry-s-portfolio-ivory.vercel.app

messages.content:
Hi all, I’m Bignesh, an MCA student at Ravenshaw University (India) heading towards compiler and hardware–software co-design research. I’m solo, in the Indie track.

Building: a loop where Muse Glimmer 30B writes its own Metal GPU kernels on my Mac Studio (M5 Max). A harness checks that each kernel gives correct results and measures whether it’s actually faster. Only measured speedups count.

Starting point (measured before kickoff, MLX, 4-bit):

decode ~26 tok/s, about 87% of the chip’s 460 GB/s memory bandwidth
prefill ~800 tok/s, nearly flat from 1K to 32K tokens
Low Power Mode makes decode 1.85× slower

There isn’t much headroom left, which makes this an honest test of whether a model can tune itself to its own hardware.

Happy to compare notes with anyone running Glimmer or Spark Open locally on Apple silicon.

messages.author: Billydavis
messages.content:
Hey everyone! I'm Billy Davis from Hudson, North Carolina.
By day, I work full time in manufacturing as a machine operator and batch maker. Outside of work, I'm an independent AI/ML researcher and the founder of Hudson Forge Technologies, a small research operation I've been building out of my home lab.
My background isn't traditional. No university degree, no professional engineering team, just determination, a strong work ethic, and five kids who motivate me to keep pushing.
Over the past several months, I've studied AI, machine learning, deep learning, LLMOps/MLOps, cybersecurity, quantum computing, and software engineering through DeepLearning.AI, NVIDIA, IBM, and Duke University's LLMOps program, and I've put that learning to work in several independent projects, including IRMB (multi-model AI research), quantum computing on real IBM hardware, Sentinel (red-team testing of my own systems), and RIP (governed research pipelines).
https://github.com/billyrdavis1985-bot
My GitHub has the repos behind all of this, including the quantum hardware work and the research pipelines:

messages.content:
Hey everyone! I’m Sunny, building Fylmer for the Meta hackathon. It’s a filmmaking workspace where a creator goes from an idea to a Film Bible, connected scenes and characters, reviewed shots, and a final cut.

Our hackathon goal is a real 30-second film made through the app. We’re integrating Muse Spark for story and shot planning and exploring SAM 3.1 for visual continuity checks. We already have a Fylmer app to build on, so the focus is making this demo work end to end.

I’m looking for teammates who enjoy Meta Model API and agent workflows, computer vision, full-stack product work, or film editing and sound. If that sounds interesting, DM me with what you’d like to build and a link to something you’ve made. We can put together a team of up to four.

messages.content:
Salam kenal semuanya! 👋

Hi everyone! I'm Edbert Taidy, a Computer Science fresh graduate from Medan, Indonesia 🇮🇩. I'm currently exploring opportunities in software engineering, and this is my second hackathon, following the NTU x Base Web3 Hackathon in Singapore!

My main tech stack includes React, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, MongoDB, and Next.js. I've also been exploring other frontend frameworks like Angular and Vue, as well as backend technologies such as Flask, Django, Spring Boot, and NestJS.

I'll be participating solo in the **Indie Developer track**, building **RoboRally: The Factory Rescue** 🤖 — an AI-powered factory maze where a robot plans actions to complete objectives, navigates obstacles, and adapts when its original plan fails. The project explores how Meta's AI models can enable more capable, goal-directed agents.

Outside of coding, I'm multilingual and enjoy connecting with people from different backgrounds and learning about different cultures. Looking forward to meeting everyone, sharing ideas, and learning together!

Senang bertemu dengan kalian semua! 🇮🇩

Looking forward to connecting with you all!

messages.author: Juhana
messages.content:
Hi all 👋 Juhana from Helsinki, Finland. Solo, Indie track.

I run a small AI company and build voice products, including a meeting transcriber for Finnish, one of the hardest languages for speech AI.

This week I'm building **Hot Seat**: a live press conference you can't prepare for. Type any company and crisis, and Muse Wonder builds the scandal. Reporters grill you out loud, interrupt when you dodge, and quote your own words back at you. Muse Voice Transcribe listens, Muse Spark watches your body language, and at the end Muse Image prints tomorrow's front page, with your face and your worst sentence as the headline.

Most leaders face their first real crisis without ever rehearsing one. English is my second language, so this also has to work for non-native speakers under pressure.

Looking for ~10 brave people to take the seat next week and tell me how it felt. Reply or DM 🎙️

messages.author: نايمار
messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋 I'm Mahfoud, a Master's student in Information Systems and developer from Algeria 🇩🇿.

I'm building **OmniGuide** — an OS-level AI companion designed to change how people interact with their computers.

The vision goes beyond traditional chat assistants: OmniGuide understands the user's screen and context, answers questions, finds relevant information, teaches workflows, and provides grounded, step-by-step visual guidance directly over the applications they're using.

For the hackathon, I'm focusing on a Linux prototype combining **Muse Spark for multimodal reasoning and contextual understanding, SAM 3.1 for visual grounding and segmentation, and a transparent desktop overlay**.

The technical challenge I'm particularly interested in is making AI guidance reliable enough to connect what the model understands with the exact elements the user sees on their screen.

Excited to build, experiment with Meta's models, and connect with other builders working on multimodal AI and intelligent agents! 🚀
https://github.com/Onee11

messages.author: Ahmaddavid_
messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋

I'm Ahmad David Fajri from Indonesia. Solo builder on the Indie track.

Background: TypeScript/React + Rust. I mostly build AI-agent tooling rather than plain apps — MotionCraft (AI-agent motion graphics on Remotion), APOS (a project-governance + continuity skill for AI-assisted coding), Fable5res (reasoning skills distilled from 4,665 real chain-of-thought traces), and Rust tooling for dependency/supply-chain policy gates. Also a bit of an AI news junkie — I try new models the week they drop.

Project: GridSense — an agent that actually operates a microgrid, not just chats about it. It reads live state (load, solar, battery, price), calls tools to charge/discharge and shed load, explains every decision in plain language, and tallies the rupiah saved. Core loop runs on Muse Spark tool-calling + Muse Image for report visuals, with Muse Spark Open via Baseten to prove the policy isn't a wrapper. Push the Frontier — energy.

Looking forward to the workshops and building with Muse Code + the full Meta stack!

GitHub: https://github.com/ahmdd4vd

messages.author: Tobagin
messages.content:
Hi everyone! I’m Thiago(Tobagin), an indie developer from Ireland with over 30 years of coding experience. I’m a full-stack developer, sysadmin and Linux enthusiast, with open-source software published in Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora repos and on Flathub. My projects range from Linux apps to networking and homelab tools—I enjoy solving problems I encounter and sharing the results.

I’m building **OpenPak**, an open-source, multi-console network where players can keep their identity, friends and community across devices, with online play supported on a game-by-game basis. It brings together accounts, friends, invitations, matchmaking, game servers and cloud saves, with Nintendo, PlayStation and Xbox platforms at different stages of development.

My next project is **Pakka**, an assistant powered by Meta’s models. Starting with selected platforms, it will help players troubleshoot through console homebrew apps and dashboards: running diagnostics, guiding repairs and verifying results.

Pakka will also collaborate with a player’s own AI agent in a shared troubleshooting session. Pakka checks OpenPak’s services while the player’s agent investigates local settings and carries out fixes with permission.

For maintainers, Pakka will combine network monitoring and player feedback to identify recurring issues and prepare bug reports and proposed fixes for review. As a solo developer, I want to spend less time repeating troubleshooting steps and more time improving the network.

OpenPak: https://github.com/openpak  
My GitHub: https://github.com/tobagin

Looking forward to meeting everyone and learning about your projects!

Hi everyone! 👋
I'm Michel, a solo AI-assisted Software Engineering student and Full-Stack Developer. Having worked as a Quality Checker (QC) for scanlation teams on Discord, I know exactly how painful and slow the manga/webtoon localization process is.
I build modern web apps using Next.js, TypeScript, FastAPI, and Python (SQLModel, Celery, Redis). I also have experience integrating AI pipelines (OCR, computer vision, and image inpainting).
I’m developing Taurge, an AI-assisted localization workspace designed for manga and webtoons. It automates text extraction, contextual translation, and background cleaning (inpainting) so translators and cleaners can work up to 3x faster.
  
For this Hackathon, I'm integrating Meta's ecosystem (like Llama 3 for intelligent translation/QC and SAM for bubble segmentation) into Taurge's async backend.

Excited to build alongside you all! 🚀

messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋 I'm Aleyna, an independent product designer from Istanbul who also builds her own tools.

I'm especially interested in responsible AI usage: using AI where it actually helps, and not burning compute on work that doesn't need it. That's the idea behind my hackathon project, a creative work hub that lets designers automate repetitive production work in design apps, no coding needed. AI creates each routine once; after that, rerunning it doesn't call the model at all.

Some things I've built before:
• efekto (beta.efekto.co): real-time image & video effects in the browser, still in development
• Pucker: a hands-free interface you control with your head and lips, which won the New Interaction category at the Figma × Contra Make-a-thon

Happy to chat about design, creative coding, and open to swapping feedback with anyone ✨

🔗 Portfolio: https://www.aleynacatak.com
🔗 LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/aleynacatak/

messages.author: kimingi27
messages.content:
Hello everyone! Excited to be here building with Meta's tools.
I'm building Vibe-debug, a debugging buddy for developers, especially vibe coders.
Broken code or pipelines and don't know where to start? What about silent failures, where something goes wrong without an obvious crash? Debugging can quickly become a nightmare, especially when you're still learning.
Vibe-debug helps developers trace function calls, capture errors and silent failures, map project components, and investigate what went wrong through a CLI, trace dashboard, and IDE integrations.

I'm exploring how Meta's models can make debugging more interactive by turning recorded failure data into clear, natural-language explanations  helping developers understand not just where something failed, but what to investigate next. Further ahead, I want to explore how natural-language interfaces and AI tools could make building and deploying software more accessible to people with different levels of technical experience.
My longer-term vision is to explore how these ideas could extend beyond software pipelines to more complex systems, including industrial processes and robotics, where observability and fault diagnosis are essential. 
I'm here to build, experiment, learn from the community, and push Vibe-debug further with Meta's tools.

Let's make debugging more understandable and building with technology more accessible.

I'm exploring how Meta's models can make debugging more interactive by turning recorded failure data into clear, natural-language explanations  helping developers understand not just where something failed, but what to investigate next. Further ahead, I want to explore how natural-language interfaces and AI tools could make building and deploying software more accessible to people with different levels of technical experience.
My longer-term vision is to explore how these ideas could extend beyond software pipelines to more complex systems, including industrial processes and robotics, where observability and fault diagnosis are essential. 
I'm here to build, experiment, learn from the community, and push Vibe-debug further with Meta's tools.

Let's make debugging more understandable and building with technology more accessible.

messages.author: Jamejobs
messages.content:
Hi everyone! I'm Sean, a product designer based in the SF Bay Area. I run a small design studio, XYZ Design, where I prototype most of my own work with 3D printing. My outdoor follow-cart concept, Summit, won a Red Dot Design Concept Award this year.

I'm here because I believe AI can do a lot more for designers than it does today. In the past two weeks I built two web-based games and two web-based synths with AI-assisted coding. The quality still has room to grow, but it made me realize I can be a "full-stack designer": someone who designs everything from the outer form to the components inside. AI made that possible.

For this hackathon I want to test what Meta's models (Muse Spark + SAM 3.1) can do with real hardware: adding a perception and voice layer to my Summit prototype so the cart can recognize its owner, read the terrain, and complete the self-following system.

This is my first hackathon and I'm really excited to be here. If you're working on robotics, embedded systems, or anything hardware-related, I'd love to connect.
GitHub: https://github.com/SYXMadeit

messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋 I'm Sahaj, a student at Sanjay Ghodawat University, Kolhapur, India 🇮🇳

🛠️ **What I work with:** Python, FastAPI, React + TypeScript, React Native, Supabase, and AI agents. I recently built an open-source AI desktop assistant with multi-LLM support, memory and an agent planner.

📚 **What I'm building: MotherTongue Books**
Children learn to read best in their mother tongue, but most of the world's languages have very few children's books, because publishing in smaller languages isn't profitable. UNESCO estimates that around **40% of people worldwide don't have access to education in a language they understand.**

I'm building an app that creates original, illustrated children's books in a child's own language (starting with Telugu, Kannada and Marathi), using:
• **Muse Spark** to write stories natively in each language (not translated)
• **Muse Image** for illustrations
• **SAM 3.1** so kids can tap objects in pictures to learn words
• **Muse Voice Transcribe** for read-aloud practice
• **Llama Guard** to keep everything child-safe

Excited to build with you all! 🚀
🐙 GitHub: github.com/Sahaj1207
🐦 X: x.com/sahaj0712

messages.content:
Hi everyone! 

I’m **Malahim Mavoungou**, Founder & Enterprise AI Architect at **Omnesight** (based between Dakar & Paris/international).

**What I'm building for this Hackathon:**
**Omnesight Sentinel** — an autonomous operational intelligence engine & Supervised Action Protocol (SAP) designed for mission-critical physical infrastructure (energy pipelines, SCADA networks, industrial supply chains).

 **How we use Meta models:**
We are building natively on the **Meta Llama Stack**, pairing **Llama 3.2 Vision (11B/90B)** with numerical SCADA sensor streams for real-time mechanical anomaly detection, cross-correlated with enterprise contractual liabilities (Take-or-Pay penalties, bank guarantees). Rather than passive chatbot text, our agents formulate deterministic, schema-validated actions gated by a cryptographic supervisory approval protocol.

**Track:** Startups Track ("Push the Frontier" problem statement)

Excited to push open-weight AI to mission-critical operations! Feel free to connect or drop a message if you are exploring enterprise agentic runtimes or physical system monitoring.

Happy building to all!

messages.author: Martin Tembo
messages.content:
Hey everyone 👋 I'm Martin Tembo, a Lead Software Engineer based in Kitwe, Zambia. I recently finished a BSc in Bioinformatics at Copperbelt University, so I sit right between the lab bench and the codebase.

What I bring:
Full-stack and systems work in TypeScript, Go, Python and Rust, with 4+ years shipping production software
Mobile apps in React Native and Expo (I built ShaftFitters, which is live on the App Store and Google Play)
AI and LLM integration: RAG, multi-provider streaming chat, voice with ElevenLabs, and, Backend architecture with Clean Architecture/DDD, Postgres and Prisma, WebSockets, and AWS (Lambda, S3)

What I'm building: Lab Assistant AI 🧪
It's an AI lab partner for researchers and students. You can store and version lab protocols, then run them as tracked experiments that go from planned to in progress to completed. You can also upload results like gel images, western blots and microscopy shots, and get AI analysis, troubleshooting and protocol tips back.

The part I'm most excited about is real-time guidance during live experiments. The phone camera and mic stream to the backend over WebSockets, an AI model watches and listens, and it talks you through each step with voice feedback.

The stack is Bun, Hono, Prisma/Postgres, AI model, ElevenLabs TTS, and S3, with a React Native Expo client.

My build: an AI for each owner that knows their one pet — dog, cat, bird or something more exotic. Hi everyone! I'm Elodie  from New York — product designer by day, dog mom and new mom always. Building solo in the Indie track.

Background: I design data and knowledge-graph systems for education, science and talent, and I ship AI side projects — a budgeting pal for families with babies, a PhD-application helper, and an offline résumé-verification Skill for an AI NAS.

My build: an AI for each owner that knows their one pet — dog, cat, bird or something more exotic. Every pet gets its own stable profile and long-term memory, and the AI only talks about that animal: records and reminders, a photo timeline with SAM 3.1, voice notes you can dictate one-handed, and travel and housing planning with sourced rules. It keeps records and points to the vet; it never gives medical advice. My first user is Coco, my 4-year-old Labrador — with a baby at home, my hands are always full.

Happy to swap notes on Muse Spark, SAM 3.1 and agent memory. 🐾

Hi Everyone,,
Anurag this side. 

Working in advance analytics in Fintech throughout.

Looking forward to meeting you all and working alongside you at this hackathon

Track - Indie

Building: WhatsApp Forward Court, a multi-agent fact-checker for viral forwards. You forward a message to a WhatsApp number, and two Muse Spark agents debate whether it’s true or false, each citing live sources. A judge agent returns a verdict card (True / False / Misleading / Unverified) in your language. It handles text, links, images and video, using Muse Spark vision and SAM 3.1 with reverse image search to catch real footage with a false story attached.

Before this: I’ve been built multi-agent systems at work and on my own projects:

AI governance tool :  I worked on an AI governance tool for banking, using ML, RAG and big data.

Currently building - 
Offline Agent Studio  is an open-source framework for building and running agents offline on local models. It has an agent builder UI. A triage agent routes tasks, a PM agent splits work across worker agents, and a verifier and test bench check the results.

Building MarketX  is a market intelligence tool for Indian equities. Agents analyses corporate announcements, news and technicals. Bull and bear agents debate, and a judge produces probabilistic picks that a validation agent checks against actuals every day.

Open to collaborating on multi-agent projects, whether that’s agent orchestration, debate and verification setups, or evaluation. Happy to team up or swap ideas.

messages.author: Bolouvi Pierre Florent
messages.content:
Hi everyone!

I’m Pierre Florent Bolouvi, founder of HOUETOR, a small tech studio based in Natitingou, Benin.

What I’m building for this hackathon:
HOUETOR lets a shop, NGO or training business update its WordPress website by writing a plain-language request, such as “change the price of this product” or “add an event on Saturday”. The agent edits the page directly, keeps a revision of every change, and can be reverted in one click. The WordPress connector plugin, Houetor Connect, was just approved and published on the official WordPress.org plugin directory.

How we use Meta models:
Our agent works through a set of 32 tools on an MCP server, so the model only has to pick the right tool call. During the hackathon I want to test the Meta Model API as an alternative reasoning engine behind the same tools, and compare tool-call accuracy and cost on the same set of real editing tasks.

Track: Startups Track

I’m also interested in hearing from people working on agentic tools for non-technical users, especially in West Africa. Feel free to connect or send me a message!

Happy building to everyone!

​What I’m building: A voice-first, multimodal task & focus engine built to solve cognitive overload for founders, individuals with ADHD, overwhelmed professionals, and chronic procrastinators.

​Brain Dump to Single Focus: Instead of overwhelming you with a massive to-do list, it lets you completely empty your head of raw thoughts, voice notes, and snapshot images. The AI intelligently processes the mental load and surfaces only the single most appropriate task for your current context, energy, and time.

​Omnipresent Capture: Seamlessly synced across WhatsApp, smartwatch/wearables, mobile, and web so you can capture thoughts instantly without losing focus.

​Meta AI Stack: Muse Voice Transcribe for frictionless voice dumps, Muse Spark for intent extraction & context mapping, SAM 3.1 for visual task capture, and Muse Code for automated execution agents.

​Skills I bring: End-to-end system architecture, real-time cross-platform syncing (wearables/bots/mobile), and automated background pipeline engineering.

​Excited to build alongside everyone!

messages.author: iolaire
messages.content:
Hi all, I'm an Arlington, VA USA retired data scientist coding 6–8 hours a day as time permits on projects that I want to use. I'm very happy that I don't need to create something that will generate money... For this hackathon, I'm converting my existing project Vedfolnir (https://vedfolnir.org/) (Your AI-powered tool for creating accessible, engaging content for the Fediverse.) to use Meta models rather than AWS Nova Lite2 models. That’s generating alt text for images and hashtags for the posts. AWS's Nova Lite models are extremely affordable, so it will be interesting to see how Meta compares. I'm also interested in seeing if Meta's hashtags are superior, given that Meta is a social media company.

But what I spend my time on this year is Vegrún (https://vegrún.com), a multimodal travel mapping platform (Vegrún helps you design multimodal trips across roads, trails, water, rail, bus, and flight, then turn them into shareable maps and export-ready visuals.) This fills a need for me as I grew up on the water and have taken River Cruises the past two years, and the big mapping systems don't do water routing. So I'm building a travel mapping platform that allows me to mix and match transit types beyond just road, bus, walking, and driving. Now I can map my flight from the US to Europe, a train ride to the mountains and back, and then down the Danube River and flights back to the US.

This most important thing with AI coding I've learned this year is that it’s best to give AI a goal like run in X seconds/minutes/hours rather than asking to make it faster. If it has a time goal that is way faster than the current timing, it will figure out how to do it. With asking to make it faster, it just does minor improvements.

messages.content:
Hi all, I’m Jaime, solo in the Indie track. I’m doing an MSc in Computational Applied Maths at Edinburgh, and my background is CS plus quant research (my thesis was an ML portfolio-optimisation backtest, published on SSRN).

Building: Market Arena, a “wind tunnel for markets”. It’s a simulated exchange where Muse Spark agents trade against each other. Market makers learn to quote, takers invent their own strategies as code (each one tested out of sample before it trades), and everything is benchmarked against optimal market-making theory. The headline question: do AI market makers learn to tacitly collude, and which exchange rules stop it?

Happy to chat about LOB simulation, agent tool-calling, or quant stuff.

messages.author: angaritarad
messages.content:
Hi everyone! I'm Miguel, a radiologist in Bogotá, Colombia, with ~25 years reading CT/MRI/ultrasound and ~10 years writing software. Competing solo in the Startups track.

The problem I know firsthand: at 3 a.m. on call, radiologists drown in software, not in images. Clicking through worklists, templates and forms is where mistakes slip in, like a "normal" template signed on an abnormal study.

For this hackathon I'm building RadMesh AI Mode: the RIS/PACS disappears as is now and becomes a conversation with an AI on-call resident. Muse Glimmer runs on the hospital's own node (open weights, no patient data egress). It prepares cases, drafts and discusses reports, and a fine-tuned QC agent catches mechanical report errors before signature. The radiologist decides and signs, always. Synthetic data only during the event.

Looking forward to the Verifiable Agents session, and glad to trade tips on serving Glimmer on Modal or LoRA fine-tuning. Good luck all! 🩻

Let's connect: https://www.linkedin.com/in/angaritarad/

messages.author: Oluwadotun Ilesanmi
messages.content:
Hi Everyone, 

I'm Dennis, a Python Developer, Data Analyst building Synk.  The context layer for fragmented workflows. 

Track: Indie Developer Track. 

What I'm building: Synk. The context layer for fragmented workflows. A major problem it'd solve is context loss/reconstruction knowledge workers experience every day. Much of our work is carried out across different tools, and we have to be the layer that connects context these across tools to get work done, reducing in cognitive overload especially for people that do high-context work daily. Synk solves this by being the layer that connects context across your workflows. It stays aware of what you're doing, maintains context across your workflows, and helps you make progress on high-context work without rebuilding context or re-explaining yourself to AI. 

<@376448514940731394>, we seem to be building something similar. Let's team up.

LinkedIn: linkedin.com/cyberrock
X: Cyber_rock

Happy to connect with y'all

messages.author: Penny Pasta 🍝
messages.content:
Hey hackers,

My names Penelope. You can call me Penny. 

I decided to enter into journalism last year. I modeled the newsroom I am still building to be for and by working class people. Not shareholders or the highest bidder for ad space. It has grown, one of the first problems I saw is the need for access to intelligence in order to break news faster. All of the tools I found online were thousands of dollars a month for access. I set out to change that. I have been testing machine learning based logic scrapers since then. I have found a reputiable 120 api's or raw file dumps that update at-least 100 times a day. I ingested that data to study how an ontology would work in realtime for newsrooms. So far, it has worked. AI has been within the journalism and newsroom fields for decades now, but we are seeing a scale like never before. I have been testing different models and building tools for researchers, journalists and newsrooms.

I entered the hackathon to showcase a ai powered ontology that is a live intelligence hub for breaking the news faster. 

https://www.instagram.com/atransjournalist?obrf=MWV5dTM0ZWpyMzJnaQ%3D%3D&utm_source=qr

https://github.com/pennytir

messages.author: Sohail
messages.content:
Hi everyone! 👋 I’m an oncology clinician working in an area with significant social deprivation and a very diverse patient population.

One challenge I see in practice is that cancer patients may struggle to communicate their symptoms clearly to clinical teams, particularly when English isn’t their first language.

For this hackathon, I’m exploring how AI could help patients report their symptoms in whichever language they are most comfortable speaking, while helping clinicians receive the relevant information in a clear and structured way. The aim is to reduce language and communication barriers and make access to acute oncology advice safer and easier.

I’m particularly interested in multilingual AI, RAG, clinical safety and human-in-the-loop systems, and would love to connect with anyone working in these areas.

Looking forward to meeting everyone and building! 🚀

messages.author: vermaPank
messages.content:
Hi everyone! I'm Pankaj, participating solo in the Indie Developer track under Build for Your World.

My project idea is ProofPath: turning a plain-language browser requirement into a test plan proposed by a Meta model, reviewed by a human, and executed with Playwright. The goal is to produce PASS, FAIL, or INCONCLUSIVE findings backed by screenshots, observed values, and replay steps.

For the hackathon, I'm keeping the scope focused on a controlled checkout demo: catch a seeded quantity/total bug, show the evidence, then rerun after the fix. The PRD and development plan are drafted; implementation is still ahead.

I'd love to connect with people working on browser automation, practical QA, or verifiable AI agents, and swap feedback as we build. Looking forward to seeing everyone's projects!

messages.author: Ruth
messages.content:
Hey everyone! 
I’m Ruthwik, from Andhra Pradesh, India, building solo.
I’m building Snapdesk, customer support that can see. A customer sends a photo of a damaged item with a text or voice message, and SAM 3.1 finds the damage and measures it.
Muse Spark then reads the business’s own policy and decides: refund, replace, repair, or hand over to a human.
If a case is unclear or the order value is high, plain code sends it to a person, so the AI never has the last word on money.
Every case ends with the marked-up photo, the measurements, the decision, and the policy line it followed. 

Excited to see what you all build!

messages.author: abberdeen
messages.content:
Hello everyone! My name is Abdurahim, and I’m a .NET FullStack developer from Tajikistan. I’ve been using AI as a coding assistant, and only recently started working with AI models via APIs.

I’m thrilled to be part of this chat and this hackathon. Seeing so many talented professionals from all over the world—it feels like an "Ultra Music Festival" for the IT community, just in a virtual format!

I saw an ad from Meta mentioning a $1 million prize, so I applied immediately. At the time, I didn’t even know Meta had its own models—or, more specifically, that they offered an API (Muse). While waiting for my application to be approved, I decided to try out Muse Code on a project I was working on, and I found it quite impressive. I honestly didn’t expect to get accepted!

Now that I’m here among so many brilliant experts, I’m not necessarily expecting to win any prizes—but I’ve decided to build something anyway. I truly hope I can create something functional and useful over these next 10 days.

Good luck to everyone—I hope you all manage to bring your ideas to life on time! https://github.com/abberdeen/

Hey everyone! 👋

I'm a software developer from Sofia, Bulgaria, with around 15 years of experience in game development, mobile apps, and backend systems. Over the past year, I've been transitioning into machine learning engineering, focusing on PyTorch and computer vision.

For this hackathon, I'm building PetSafe Plants, an AI-powered assistant that helps pet owners identify potentially toxic plants.

The idea comes from personal experience. My cat became ill after drinking water from a vase containing lilies, and I wanted to build something that could help other pet owners avoid similar situations.

I'm planning to combine Meta's vision and segmentation models to identify plants, investigate uncertain predictions, and detect potentially dangerous plants even in mixed bouquets.

Looking forward to experimenting with Meta's models, learning from everyone, and seeing what you all build!

My portfolio: https://vmirchev.com

messages.author: Daniel
messages.content:
👋 Hey everyone! I’m Daniel from Lagos, Nigeria 🇳🇬, an MLOps/AI engineer working on production ML for climate risk, forecasting and agentic systems. I’m also the IT/cloud lead at a Nigerian microfinance bank.

Building: 🌊 FloodLens, an agent that checks flood risk on loan collateral for African microfinance lenders. It segments Sentinel-2 satellite imagery with SAM 3.1, then Muse Spark reasons over water extents, elevation and rainfall history to give loan officers an explained risk tier and a lending recommendation. Every rainy season in Lagos, borrowers and their collateral go underwater together, and lenders have no way to price that risk.

Track: Indie
Stack: Python, FastAPI, Sentinel Hub, AWS / Modal

Happy to swap notes with anyone working on satellite/geospatial, climate, or fintech, or anyone else building from Africa. Let’s build! 🚀

GitHub: github.com/jemiridaniel · LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/jemiridanieltaiwo

It segments Sentinel-2 satellite imagery with SAM 3.1, then Muse Spark reasons over water extents, elevation and rainfall history to give loan officers an explained risk tier and a lending recommendation. Every rainy season in Lagos, borrowers and their collateral go underwater together, and lenders have no way to price that risk.

Track: Indie
Stack: Python, FastAPI, Sentinel Hub, AWS / Modal

Happy to swap notes with anyone working on satellite/geospatial, climate, or fintech, or anyone else building from Africa. Let’s build! 🚀

messages.author: Docdrewbe
messages.content:
Hey everyone! I’m Doc—Docdrewbe here. I’m an older entrepreneur learning to build software with AI teaching me along the way, and I don’t do idle very well. 😂

Going through cancer has sharpened my sense of what I want to spend my time on. For me, that means building something useful—something that can help lower-income communities and rural critical access hospitals do more with the resources they have

For this hackathon, I’m building a tool that takes complex compliance requirements and makes them easier to understand and work through. The goal is to help organizations see where they meet requirements, where gaps remain, and what needs attention—with the supporting information to understand why.

Hospitals are the starting point. The backbone is being designed to support other highly regulated industries, so the same approach can help people navigate different requirements without rebuilding everything from scratch.

It won’t make decisions for people. It will help them make informed decisions by putting the requirements, evidence, and next steps within reach. For organizations with limited staff and resources, I believe that could make a meaningful difference.

I bring the vision, determination, and willingness to learn. I’m building openly and would welcome collaborators, technical guidance, or perspectives from people familiar with hospital operations and compliance. Even helping me think through a difficult piece would be appreciated.

Looking forward to meeting you, learning what you’re building, and finding ways to help each other!

Hi everyone! 👋

I'm Syed, a solo founder based in Parker, Colorado. 

My project is VerbaGPT (https://app.verbagpt.com/): ask questions about your data in plain English, and it writes the SQL or Python, runs it, and gives you charts and answers and deep insights from complex databases. 

Background: healthcare actuary, 20 years in healthcare analytics and complex actuarial modeling. 

For this hackathon, I'm integrating Muse Spark through the Meta Model API as a first-class model to query cloud and local databases. I'm also using Meta's vision modality to reproduce entire data analysis from just an image or snapshot. 

I'm particularly interested in connecting with people working on natural-language-to-SQL, agentic data analysis, local and private AI, the Meta Model API, and security for AI apps. Happy to swap feedback as we build.

🔗 LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/smehmud

Looking forward to seeing what everyone makes! 🚀

messages.author: Boon How
messages.content:
👋 Hi all — I'm BH (Boon-How Chew), a family medicine professor and clinical researcher at Universiti Putra Malaysia, in Kuala Lumpur (GMT+8, so I'll be the one awake at odd hours).

**What I bring:** clinical epidemiology and research methodology, plus a habit of shipping self-contained HTML/JS tools that run with no backend.

**What I'm building:** an agentic verification layer for scientific manuscripts. Papers today are accepted or rejected largely on reviewer intuition — almost nobody checks whether the reported numbers, the stated methods, and the deposited data actually agree. I want agents that read a manuscript alongside its data and code and produce an audit a human can contest: every claim traced to evidence, with a separately instantiated challenge agent (no authoring history, so it isn't anchored by what it helped write) arguing the other side.

Planning on Muse Spark for the reasoning/orchestration and Muse Code to build fast.

Solo for now, open to teaming up. Ping me if research integrity is your thing 🙂

Hey everyone — I'm Krish Adavi (Texas). i built a2zai.ai. 

I am going to work on the problem below for this hackathon. 

Problem: AI agents now do real work everywhere, but nobody can verify an agent did the job well. Demos are staged, benchmarks get gamed, receipts don't exist.

A2ZAI Lab is the trust layer: exams built from real work, graded against a checked answer key, scores and full evidence published. A driving test for AI agents.

First exam: catch the money-laundering pattern hidden across 25 bank fraud alerts.

Background: engineering manager at AWS Security and Goldman Sachs — security apps, banking compliance and risk. Also a real-money trader.

My newsletter (24 editions out -  deep dives on building AI Systems)

messages.author: Zohaib Sharif
messages.content:
Hi all, Zohaib here, London.Most of my pain is back-office admin, and that’s what I’m attacking.

Skills: business automation and agent orchestration (n8n, multi-agent setups), self-hosted LLM infra (DGX Spark, local open weights), Python, and hands-on UK accounting/VAT workflows.

Building solo on the Indie track (“Build for Your World”): an AI-run accounting system that takes a small business from receipts and invoices through to HMRC filing with no traditional accounting package. Agents propose and categorise, the owner approves in the app, agents execute, and the owner gets daily summaries and cash forecasts. Plan: Muse Spark via the Meta Model API for reasoning and document understanding, Muse Spark Open / Muse Glimmer running locally on the DGX for the privacy-sensitive ledger work, and Muse Code to build fast.

Keen to swap notes with anyone doing fintech, agents or tax automation. 👋

messages.author: Highly_Eccentric_Orbit
messages.content:
🚀👋 Hey everyone! I'm Dan Lee-Odinson, flying solo in the Indie track as team Ad Astra Simul (to the stars, together), originally from Portland OR, currently in sunny Florida!

I work in payroll and HR software implementation, and I'm also working on a B.S. in Space Studies at Everglades University. On the side I run Project AESIR, an open-source amateur space program. Its first piece is HUGINN, a simulated CubeSat I fly by written procedure through OpenC3 COSMOS, the open-source ground system used on real missions.

My hackathon project (Push the Frontier) is ODIN, an AI mission supervisor for HUGINN. Muse Spark works the ground console, and Muse Glimmer takes over onboard when the spacecraft loses contact. Either way, every command the AI wants to send has to clear a deterministic safety gateway first. Then ODIN flies the same anomaly passes I flew, so we can see how its calls stack up against mine.

Longer term, I'm working my way into spacecraft mission operations. Looking forward to seeing what everyone ships! If you care about what AI agents should be allowed to do on their own, come say hi. 🖖

🔗 LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/dan-lee-odinson/
💻 GitHub: https://github.com/dan-lee-odinson

messages.author: Hutarajashish
messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋 I'm Ashish Adhikari from Parma, Ohio 🇺🇸

I'm building Gol — an AI backend assistant for small shop owners. No dashboards, no menus: the owner just chats, and Gol reads the sales, stages stock and book entries, drafts posts and runs the back office — the owner only approves. ("Gol" means circle in Nepali — one circle around the whole business.)

It's not a prototype: Gol is already live in production in real stores — two convenience stores here in Ohio and a client shop in Nepal — powered by the Meta Model API (Muse Spark).

Track: Build for Your World — Startup.

My belief: software should learn the human's language, not the other way around.

messages.author: Docdrewbe
messages.content:
Hi, I’m Drew. I bring 22 years of experience in healthcare compliance and regulatory compliance, and that experience is the knowledge base guiding what we’re building with Sentinel.

Sentinel is an AI-assisted regulatory compliance platform designed to make complex requirements easier to understand and manage. We’re starting with critical access hospitals, rural healthcare organizations, and small clinics—teams facing significant compliance responsibilities with limited resources. My role is to ground the platform in practical knowledge of how compliance works and what these organizations need.

Our hope is for Sentinel to become a trusted working partner that turns requirements into clear actions, helps organize supporting evidence, and identifies gaps before they become problems—giving teams more time to focus on the communities they serve.

Healthcare is our starting point. Once the core backbone is built, we intend to adapt the software across industries by connecting it to each sector’s regulations, standards, and workflows. Our long-term vision is to make practical, affordable compliance support accessible to organizations of every size.

messages.author: Oumy Dieng
messages.content:
Hey everyone!  Excited to be part of the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon!

 Who I am:
I’m Oumy, a Full-Stack & AI Developer passionate about building practical, human-centered AI products that bridge computer vision and real-world physical tasks.

Skills I bring:
Python (FastAPI), PostgreSQL, Multimodal AI integration, Computer Vision / AR interfaces, Web Audio signal processing, and product UX design.

What I’m planning to build (Solo — Build for Your World / Push the Frontier):
Every year, millions of household appliances (fans, coffee makers, laptops) end up as e-waste simply because everyday people aren't technicians and don't know which $5 part failed or how to safely inspect it.

For this hackathon, I’m building **RepairLens** — a multimodal visual, voice, and acoustic AI repair co-pilot powered by **Meta SAM 3.1** and **Meta Muse Spark**:
• **Visual Part Isolation (SAM 3.1)**: Point your phone at any broken appliance or tap on the screen to segment internal components and see a beginner-friendly visual guide (zero technical jargon).
• **Multimodal & Acoustic Diagnosis (Muse Spark)**: Combines visual inspection, motor sound frequency analysis, and persistent multi-day memory to guide you step-by-step.
• **Live AI Video Co-Pilot**: Real-time camera guidance during repair that distinguishes your hand, the tool you're holding, and the target appliance — while enforcing electrical safety checks.

Looking forward to building this week and seeing what everyone else creates!

messages.author: Aritra Chakraborty
messages.content:
Hey everyone!
I am Aritra Chakraborty from India. I am a product manager and an AI software building enthusiast.I am competing for the Indie Track.
I am building SafeCity Lens. Cities already collect a lot of signals, and they already have cameras, but control rooms still find out too late and have no shared, explainable way to act. SafeCity Lens gives police, fire, and hospitals one picture of a developing crowd, fire, or medical risk. The score is computed from the evidence. A policy decides whether a camera is justified, and a person approves the response. The aim is faster action with a record of why the system looked, and why it held back.

messages.author: Gletrix
messages.content:
Hey everyone, I'm Gletrix! 👋
I'm building a 3D AI rendering engine that skips meshes entirely. Traditional 3D graphics describe objects with triangles, which can limit detail and use a lot of memory. My engine calculates each pixel directly, so surfaces stay smooth at any zoom level and scenes don't need heavy geometry files.
The AI part handles those per-pixel calculations, working out color, lighting, and depth straight from the scene data. The goal is sharper, more accurate visuals with a lighter footprint.
I'm excited to be part of this hackathon and can't wait to see what everyone builds. Feel free to ask me anything about the project! 🚀

messages.content:
Blessings everyone 🙏 I'm Ahmad Odeh — solo founder of ABUZ8 LLC (Dayton, Ohio), building in the Indie track.

The honest version: I'm a one-person company. I taught myself AI this past year, and I work with a small fleet of AI agents as my team — because I believe one determined person can now build what used to take a whole company.

This week I'm building Showfront, from scratch, for a reason close to home: my brother runs a small independent dealership, and I've watched good cars sit unsold because buyers couldn't truly see them online. Showfront takes a dealer's fresh lot photos and, on its own, builds the full showroom experience — SAM 3.1 isolates the car, Muse Image builds the scene, the buyer gets an interactive 360 spin and a 3D walkaround they can explore from home, Muse Spark writes the listing, and a finished commercial for the store comes out the other end, posted everywhere automatically. His lot is my real-world test case — a real dealer judges everything I ship.

I'm here to learn as much as to compete. If you're working on 3D, imaging, or agents that do real work, I'd love to connect — and if I can help anyone with local AI setups (dual-GPU lab at home), my door is open.

messages.content:
Hi everyone! I’m Dami, joining the Indie Dev track.

I’m building Wokadi, an AI operations assistant for small businesses. It’s designed to learn each business’s workflows and vocabulary, organize incoming records, and help owners manage daily operations through familiar channels such as WhatsApp.

My first pilot is a drinks distributor whose weekly stocktaking takes a whole day. My hackathon focus is turning invoice photos and goods-received records into structured stock records, asking for clarification when needed, and producing expected-stock reports to compare with physical counts.

I plan to use the Meta Model API for business onboarding, document interpretation, and operational reasoning, with validation and human review around the outputs.
I’m also exploring an optional spatial counting tool: record a store, revisit the capture, select product stacks, and review counts.

Looking forward to exchanging ideas with fellow builders, especially around practical AI, document understanding, and computer vision!

Hello everyone!

I'm Dr. Abhirup Guha from Kolkata, India, a cybersecurity leader, researcher, and technology entrepreneur with over 15 years of experience in cybersecurity, ethical hacking, AI-driven security, and enterprise cyber defense.

For the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026, I'm building CYBERGENESIS — an Autonomous Self-Defending Digital Twin.

The idea is to create an AI-powered simulation of enterprise infrastructure where autonomous attacker and defender agents continuously challenge each other. The system will identify vulnerabilities, simulate cyberattacks, deploy intelligent countermeasures, and independently verify whether the defenses actually work.

My goal is to explore a future where cybersecurity evolves beyond passive monitoring into autonomous, adaptive, and self-healing digital infrastructure.

I'm excited to connect with fellow AI builders, researchers, and developers from around the world, exchange ideas, and explore collaborations!

GitHub: https://github.com/fir3storm

Looking forward to building something meaningful with this amazing community!

messages.author: Smeet Mehta
messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋

I’m Smeet Mehta, a third-year B.Tech CSE (AI/ML) student at VIT Chennai, from India. I’m also a solo founder, and I like building things end to end. In my spare time I draw and animate, so I care a lot about how a product feels, not just whether it works.

For this hackathon I’m entering the Indie track with FieldWitness (working name). From Kharif 2026, Indian farmers can claim insurance for wild-animal crop damage, but they have to report within 72 hours and have no good way to prove what happened. I’m using SAM 3.1 and Muse Glimmer to turn a phone video of a damaged field into a claim report with measured damaged area.

I’d really like to hear from anyone who’s worked with SAM 3.1 video tracking, or who has field or crop footage, or contacts with farmers. Happy to swap feedback and help with anything I know too.

GitHub: https://github.com/Smeetmehta27
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/smeet-mehta-025545326

Looking forward to seeing what everyone builds!

messages.author: poferraz
messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋

I'm Paulo, retail manager by day, vibe coder by night (originally from Brazil, with a culinary detour along the way). I ship real tools for my team with AI agents: dashboards, ops tools, coaching apps, even though I'm not a professional engineer.

That's exactly why I'm building **vibe-fence**: a harness that lets non-technical vibe-coders like me ship AI-built software safely. Any coding agent plugs in, and every change must pass deterministic guardrails: builds, tests, validation, before it lands. When something breaks, a **teaching dial** explains what went wrong instead of just blocking you, so you actually learn instead of copy-pasting errors back into the chat. It’s a work in progress that can change this week.

Building it for people like me: retail managers, founders, students, anyone shipping real software with AI but without a CS degree.

Would love feedback, and happy to jam with anyone working on evals, agent safety, or dev tools. Good luck, everyone! 🚀

messages.author: jrodsoto
messages.content:
Hi everyone! I'm Benny Rodriguez a solo indie dev building Road to 5K — a rehab-to-race coach for Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses.

The idea comes from my own world: I'm in physical therapy working toward my first 5K after an injury last spring season. so I'm building the coach I wish I had — it turns a PT plan into a lens coach that walks you through the session, exercise by exercise, and logs the work when you finish. Plan → Coach → Record.

I'm here in the "Build for Your World" track, learning as I build (Python and ML background, new to lens/web apps), and having fun with it. One of my previous apps development for wearables devices included an application for an exercise tracking device. Happy to swap notes, especially on agents, the Model API, and getting a lens app from a simulator to a real pair of glasses. Looking forward to building alongside you all! 🐜

Hi everyone! I'm Pavlo, a solo founder from Houston, TX 🇺🇸🇺🇦

Before tech, I was a long-haul truck driver in the US, so I know the industry from the driver's seat. Now I build apps for truckers: my app Truck Driver Helper is live on iOS and Android and helps drivers calculate their real profit per load.

For this hackathon I'm building a WhatsApp AI co-pilot for truck drivers who don't speak strong English. A driver sends a voice note in their own language plus a photo of a rate confirmation, and the bot (powered by Muse Spark) finds hidden fines, tracks detention time, and writes a professional email to the broker to get paid.

Happy to connect with anyone into logistics, voice AI, or WhatsApp bots. Good luck and happy hacking! 🚛🔥

messages.content:
Hey. Lots of great ideas and projects being posted already. Looking forward to seeing how they all play out.

My name is Joshua (or silverfire in various places online), and I'm new to the magical world of agentic coding. I've been in coding off and on for a while, completing an Intro to C course in college, participating in Google coding courses on Udacity, continuing my education with Coursera, etc. I have some more recent QA background: testing VR games and apps, including previously for Downpour Interactive and Aexlab. 

Given my experience with writing, hypnosis, and public speaking, I'm looking at making an assistant app that can look at your speech notes and outline and generate in-ear audio prompts to keep you on task during speeches, looking at the audience instead of your outline, tell when you're lagging behind your projected timing, etc. I envision it as being used either with a Bluetooth earbud or Meta Glasses. Obviously, this would be for the Build for Your World track. It might be a little ambitious for my level of experience in agentic coding and AI, but nothing ventured, nothing gained, right? 

I was originally looking at doing an in-ear hypnosis session mentor, but figured branching it out wider would be better, so it could be used in multiple fields.

Also, I'm open to collaborating or being part of a team. Can only help me learn and improve faster. 😄

GitHub: https://github.com/silverfire32

messages.author: AneudysAmparo
messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋

I'm Aneudys, a software developer from Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic 🇩🇴. I've spent 11+ years shipping software, and now I run a small software/AI studio.

For this hackathon I'm entering the Startup track, solo, with Postor — an AI copilot that helps small businesses in the Dominican Republic and USA sell to the government. Government tender dossiers here are long, legal-heavy PDFs, and most small companies never even try to bid because they can't tell if they qualify. Postor reads the dossier and gives them a plain-Spanish summary, a go/no-go verdict with citations to the exact page, and a compliance checklist with deadlines.

I'm building it on Muse Spark + SAM 3.1 — SAM for the scanned, stamped pages and tables that plain text extraction can't read.

I'd love to connect with anyone working with SAM 3.1, the Meta Model API, or document-heavy AI — and anyone into govtech or procurement. Happy to swap feedback all week!

🔗 https://postor.do
💻 https://github.com/aneudysamparo

Good luck to everyone! 🚀

messages.author: Andrii Tereshchenko
messages.content:
👋 Hi everyone, I'm Andrii Tereshchenko — founder of Andrii Co. (https://andrii.co), a mobile notary & apostille practice in Bothell, WA, and a Startup Track hacker here.

    📜 My project: the Apostille Handbook — one source for every country's apostille details and forms, kept current, with prepaid labels and envelopes delivered to your door. Starting with 106 apostille authorities across
the US, Canada, and Mexico.

messages.author: Samoxis
messages.content:
Hi all. Sorin, from the UK. Solo, Indie track, Push the Frontier.

By day I fix fibre-optic networks, which mostly involves standing in holes. By night I build things with AI, which mostly involves standing in slightly warmer holes.

This week I’m building BlinkFlow. Robots are getting cheaper, friendlier and more common. Understanding why they just walked into the furniture is not.

So: when a robot does something wrong, you simply say what you saw. BlinkFlow rewinds the screen, finds the moment, works out which part of the robot’s program is to blame, fixes it, and plays the exact same scene again to prove the problem has gone away. If the fix doesn’t work, it quietly undoes it and tries again, which is more than can be said for most of us.

The test pilot is a small open-source robot duck. Roughly eight seconds into every run, it walks into a purple box with the serene confidence of something that has never been told otherwise. 🦆

Under the hood: Muse Glimmer running locally, SAM 3.1, Muse Wonder and Muse Code. The icon is by Muse Image. It is an eye that blinks and rewinds, which is also what I do every time the duck hits the box.

Repo: https://github.com/samoxis/blinkflow

Happy to swap notes with anyone doing robots, simulators or agents. Don’t panic.

messages.author: Barbara Ackles
messages.content:
Hey everyone 👋 I'm Barbara Ackles, a solo dev from Dawson Creek, BC, Canada. I run Creative WebMatrix Solutions, a small tech consultancy for rural and remote businesses up here.
I'm building SiteSense in the indie track (Build for Your World): a field assistant for oil & gas lease operators in BC's Peace Region. It works top-down: free Sentinel-2 satellite imagery flags areas of interest, a drone survey ranks the photos worst-first, and a phone close-up runs through SAM 3.1 segmentation and Muse Wonder diagnosis to produce a severity-rated work order. Safety-first by design: it never claims to "see" gas, and it says so when confidence is low. There's also a wildfire layer built from a decade of BC Wildfire Service data, spun out of my earlier project, Emberline.
Keen to trade notes with anyone working on field or industrial inspection, satellite/drone pipelines, or tool-calling agents. Good luck, everyone!

messages.author: Tg33
messages.content:
Hey y'all a cybersecurity researcher 

My research targets a specific failure: security teams act on the wrong alerts — not because the tooling is broken, but because the metrics they optimize for don’t map to the goals they actually care about. I built the Goal Coherence Matrix to measure that gap precisely — between what a SOC says it’s optimizing for and what its metrics actually reward. 

I typically build solo but this time I’m looking to work with a team.

For this hackathon I’m extending the research into working software: using LLM to re-score and explain security alerts against an org’s actual goals instead of generic severity, so analysts get the why behind an alert, not just a number. 

GitHub: [www.github.com/wellytg](https://github.com/wellytg) | LinkedIn: [linkedin.com/in/wellingtongwavava](https://www.linkedin.com/in/wellingtongwavava/)

Happy to connect with anyone working on security, agents, or applied AI.

Hey everyone! 👋 I'm an indie developer excited to join the Meta AI Developer Hackathon!

My background includes Unity/game development, Windows desktop software, web applications, and AI-assisted engineering using Claude Code, Codex, and soon Muse Code.

Hello everyone! 👋

I'm Babajide Ibiayo, a software engineer, technology entrepreneur and programming educator based in Lagos, Nigeria. I'm also a postgraduate Information Technology student at MIVA Open University.
