messages.author: Billyhill
messages.content:
Hello everyone!
I’m Michael, and for the past 8 years, I’ve been running Cup-Holster, a company I founded to solve a pretty simple problem: giving your drink a dedicated place to live at your desk. Since then, Cup-Holster has helped over 100,000 customers keep drinks off their workspaces, preventing spills and saving countless laptops and keyboards. It’s even found its way into places I never anticipated, from hospitals and medical settings to moms walking on treadmills!
I started the business while studying computer science in college, so technology has always been a big part of my background. Over the years, I’ve developed various software tools to help manage my business and simplify day-to-day operations. But one area I’ve always wanted to explore further is robotics and hardware automation.
With how far AI has come, I think we're at an exciting point where AI and robotics can start making a real difference for small businesses like mine. My goal over the next 10 days is to explore that intersection and hopefully build something that reduces some of the physical work involved in running a physical products business.
As the founder of a Made-in-the-U.S.A. products business based in Washington State, I'm excited to see what I can build with Meta's AI tools and what everyone else comes up with along the way.
Looking forward to meeting you all, and good luck everyone!

messages.author: Simeon Aldana
messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋 I'm Simeon, a software engineer and co-founder of Hipócrates, a healthcare AI startup serving clinics across Latin America.

I'm building this alongside my co-founder, Dr. Luis Piñerua, who brings the medical expertise while I lead engineering, product, and AI development.

For this hackathon, we're building an AI-powered Patient Continuity Engine using Meta's models and a multi-agent architecture. The idea is to connect clinical records, appointment scheduling, and WhatsApp to proactively identify and reconnect patients who need follow-up care.

For example, imagine a diabetic patient who hasn't attended a follow-up appointment in six months. Our AI identifies the gap in care, reaches out via WhatsApp, and helps the patient schedule a new appointment before preventable complications arise, following clinician-defined protocols.

We already have a healthcare platform running in production with paying clinics, giving us the opportunity to test and validate this technology in real clinical environments.

Our mission is simple: **No patient left behind. No critical follow-up forgotten.**

Excited to meet everyone and see what you're building! 🚀

https://hipocratesalud.com/

messages.author: Mario Vilnius
messages.content:
Hello everyone! 👋 I'm Marius Pareščius from Vilnius, Lithuania 🇱🇹 — a cybersecurity and defence tech advisor, startup mentor and serial entrepreneur.

At the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon I'm building **Operacija Dvina** 🚀 — a youth audio quest about Plokštinė, a Soviet underground nuclear missile base hidden in a Lithuanian forest, now the Cold War Museum. Remote episodes hook you at home; at the museum, QR codes on the walls unlock missions, quizzes and "Legend or fact?" cards built from local witnesses' memories.

The twist: AI guides invent facts, so ours can't. Muse Wonder writes only from official sources and named testimonies, every sentence carries its source, and a verifier fails the build if any quote or number can't be found. Muse Spark translates it into 11 languages.

Happy to swap notes on grounding/verification, small-language TTS (Lithuanian!) and getting Muse's long reasoning to fit tight token budgets. Happy hacking!

Hello everyone! 👋 I'm Marius Pareščius from Vilnius, Lithuania 🇱🇹 — a cybersecurity and defence tech advisor, startup mentor and serial entrepreneur.

At the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon I'm building **Operacija Dvina** 🚀 — a youth audio quest about Plokštinė, a Soviet underground nuclear missile base hidden in a Lithuanian forest, now the Cold War Museum. Remote episodes hook you at home; at the museum, QR codes on the walls unlock missions, quizzes and "Legend or fact?" cards built from local witnesses' memories.

The twist: AI guides invent facts, so ours can't. Muse Wonder writes only from official sources and named testimonies, every sentence carries its source, and a verifier fails the build if any quote or number can't be found. Muse Spark translates it into 11 languages.

Happy to swap notes on grounding/verification, small-language TTS (Lithuanian!) and getting Muse's long reasoning to fit tight token budgets. Happy hacking!

messages.author: Tracy
messages.content:
👋 Hey everybody!

I'm Tracy — a software engineer from Zambia 🇿🇲, and I'm building **Agrisense**
for the indie track. Looking for one or more partners to build it with!

Here's the problem: most Zambian smallholders farm entirely on rain, and El Niño
is making that rain wildly unpredictable. So planting decisions still get made by
word of mouth and memory — which is exactly the wrong tool for a climate that keeps
changing its mind. Agrisense turns a forecast into a plain-language "plant / wait /
harvest now" answer, delivered in a local dialect. It's the kind of project I'm genuinely
excited to work on because it's for my world. 🌽

Stack so far: Node.js · React · PostgreSQL — API already built and deployed, just need to build on top of it.

Looking for someone who:
• is happy shipping fast this week over perfecting later
• can own one their work cleanly 

If any of that sparked something, DM me! Happy to share the repo early and geek out
over the details. 🚀

messages.author: ZenlessZ
messages.content: Hey everyone, I'm Aryan Chettri from India, I'm currently a second year student at Manipal University Jaipur. Been competing in lots of hackathons and community events recently, excited to connect and learn here.     Here's the problem: satellites can only scan the surface skin of the ocean, but the real climate engine is hidden hundreds of meters deep. In the North Indian Ocean—where subsurface heat supercharges cyclones and dictates monsoon rains—physical sensors like Argo floats are hundreds of kilometers apart, leaving massive blind spots. OceanScope AI uses deep learning to 'see through' the surface, turning satellite altimetry and wind dynamics into full daily 3D subsurface temperature maps down to 1,000 meters. It's the kind of project I'm genuinely excited to work on because the ocean beneath the surface shapes our world. 🌊      Looking for someone who's interested in this project and willing to work at all.   If anyone's interested, hit me up.

messages.author: Bibek
messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋 I’m Bibek Sarkar, a full-stack AI developer from India teaming up with @Dona (Bhashwati Roy) in the Indie Developer Track!

We’re building **SnapPart** under the *Push the Frontier (Manufacturing & Physical Systems)* theme — an autonomous visual-to-parametric reverse-engineering pipeline. You snap a photo of a broken or spare mechanical bracket next to a reference coin, and SnapPart uses **Meta SAM 3.1** for sub-millimeter contour segmentation and **Muse Spark** to synthesize executable **CadQuery** Python code, outputting a 3D-printable `.STL` and interactive `.GLTF` solid body in seconds.

I’m handling the FastAPI backend, OpenCV geometry math, and CadQuery/Meta API orchestration. Super pumped to build alongside everyone here! 🚀

Hi everyone! 👋 I’m Bhashwati Roy, joining from India and partnering with @Bibek in the Indie Developer Track to build **SnapPart** ("Snap a photo, print a part").

messages.author: Laszlo
messages.content:
Hey everyone! I’m Laszlo from Hungary, and I’ve been building on the internet for over 25 years. Right now, I’m focused on domain-specific agentic systems and running my own self-improving software factory (https://watt-mind.github.io/factory/).

I maintain a couple of vertical AI platforms: Coach Watts (https://coachwatts.com), an open-source AI endurance coach, and LegalEase (https://legalease.hu), an agentic workspace for Hungarian attorneys that I recently launched.

For my next project, I’m leaning toward building an open-source LLM proxy for text and image PII masking. That said, I’m torn between two other ideas: an autonomous guardian agent that remediates security issues on home/family networks, or a decentralized agent-to-agent ledger where personal agents can coordinate and settle tasks directly.

Hey everyone! 👋 Pam here from Ventura County, California.

I have spent the last 5 years as an integration engineer connecting SaaS and ERP systems. I basically make apps talk to each other that were never meant to. Lately i've been building human-in-the-loop AI agents.

For this hackathon i'm building Physical MCP: giving machines that have buttons and a screen but no API an actual API, so an agent can run them. a webcam + SAM 3.1 finds the buttons, Muse Code writes the MCP server, and a little servo finger presses them. yes, a robot finger.

My background is all backend/APIs/agents, so if you're a frontend person, or you just want to film a robot finger pressing buttons, come say hi! Solo right now, open to a team of 2-3. PT timezone. THANK U!! 🙏

messages.author: Lydia &P
messages.content:
Hi, I'm Lydia Terry. I run Ampersand Prep, where I teach SAT/ACT prep, and I wrote The Good Student's Guide to Bad Tests.

I'm on the startup track and I am absolutely building for my world.

This project was born out of necessity. The SAT, by its very nature, is very good at recognizing students who use cognitive agency, common sense, and critical thinking... at least at the high end. However, like most spaces these days, AI tutoring has flooded the market and not in a good way. I think this is the opposite of what we want because agentic thinking in the age of AI is the right role for humans, as AI can handle the algorithmic thinking.

All the AI tools, even the best models, can solve most SAT problems but can't understand or explain why it's difficult for a human, primarily because it can't replicate human bias. Because bias can be thought of as a heuristic understood to be a rule, I am trying to use the predictive nature of AI to recognize bias by using an agent stack.

I am new to this space, but I have some success thus far.

My hope is this can help ed tech with higher-quality AI tools with a pedagogical purpose rather than a completion purpose.

I'd love to talk with anyone working on LLM judges, AI evaluation, assessment design, or K-12 learning tools.

LinkedIn:linkedin.com/in/lydiaterry
Website: www.ampersandprep.com

messages.author: William Chong
messages.content:
Hey everyone, William here from Singapore.

I helped to build SourceTruth.io, a canonical text API across 30 corpora of religious, philosophical, and classical texts (Quran, Bible translations, Bhagavad Gita, Confucian works, Sanskrit, Classical Chinese).

For this hackathon I'm taking that corpus work into a harder context: the Singapore End-of-Life Companion. Voice-enabled spiritual guide for dying patients and their families, 9 traditions, 4 languages including Hokkien and Cantonese via SeamlessM4T v2.

The architecture is a four-model tiered pipeline: Muse Glimmer for tradition classification and intent routing, Spark Open for generation, Wonder for deep theological edge cases (distinguishing Theravada from Mahayana funeral practice, staying inside Taoist cosmology without importing Buddhist concepts), Voice Transcribe for English/Mandarin STT. Four compliance gates: PII screening, crisis escalation to SOS Singapore, interfaith harmony checking, hallucination grounding.

The domain punishes errors. A model that invents a death ritual causes real harm in a clinical setting. Every response cites its source passage, but the hard work is the routing and compliance layer, not the retrieval.

Happy to compare notes on multilingual voice pipelines, tradition-aware routing, or interfaith NLP. Deadline Nov 4.

👋 Hey everyone!

I’m an aspiring AI/ML Engineer, and I’m excited to be participating in this hackathon!

🚀 Meet MAVIS — Your AI-Powered Personal Productivity Assistant!

I’m building MAVIS, a conversational AI assistant designed to help people manage their daily lives through natural voice and text interactions.

🧠 What MAVIS will do:

* 🎙️ Understand voice and text commands
* 📅 Help manage calendars and daily schedules
* ⏰ Create reminders and organize tasks
* 📧 Assist with emails and everyday workflows
* 💾 Maintain persistent memory for personalized assistance
* 🤖 Proactively help users stay organized and productive

Tech Stack: Python, Flask, AI language models, speech-to-text, APIs, and database integration.

My Goal: Build an intelligent assistant that goes beyond answering questions and actually helps people take action, manage responsibilities, and simplify their everyday lives.

I’m challenging myself to build something that’s not only functional and innovative but also exciting enough that people genuinely want to try it, share it, and talk about it!

I’m still early in my AI engineering journey, but I’m ready to push myself, learn from this incredible community, and bring MAVIS to life.

I’d love to connect with fellow builders, exchange ideas, and hear your feedback!

Let’s build something unforgettable! 🚀🔥

messages.author: Makabeez
messages.content:
👋 Hey everyone — I’m Joe (Aymen), based in Geneva 🇨🇭

Who I am: Managing Director in air cargo by day, algorithmic trader and solo Web3/AI builder by night. Ex-prop trader (funding-rate basis, delta-neutral strategies), so most of what I build sits where AI agents meet markets.

Skills I bring:

AI agents and LLM pipelines (tool use, eval harnesses, confidence gating)
Trading systems: backtesting, signal infra, execution on Hyperliquid and other DEXs
Full-stack: Python, TypeScript/Next.js, Solidity, self-hosted infra
Recent work: a public prompt-injection benchmark for news-driven trading agents (jev-news-bench)

What I’m building: Falsify, an agent that tries to kill your trading ideas before the market does. You give it a thesis (“BTC pumps after X”, “this funding spread mean-reverts”), and it designs tests, pulls the data, and tries to refute it, then hands back a verdict with the evidence. Most tools confirm your bias. This one is built to break it.

Going Indie track, solo. Happy to swap feedback with anyone working on agents, evals, or finance. DMs open 🤝

GitHub: github.com/Makabeez · X: @GeiserJoe2

messages.author: TA
messages.content: Hi all, Thomas here, solo Indie Dev entry. My world is clinical trial programming: pharma holds millions of lines of legacy SAS and is moving to R, but every translated program has to produce numerically identical results for regulators. I'm building an agent on Muse Spark via the Meta Model API, with Muse Spark Open as the open-weight comparison, that translates a SAS program, runs both versions, compares the output datasets and tables, and repairs the R code from the differences until they match. Benchmark: 100 open-source clinical SAS programs with a published leaderboard of translation accuracy and equivalence rates. Happy to compare notes with anyone doing code migration or verification agents.

messages.author: Clippify
messages.content:
Hey all, Irfan here from Australia 👋 I run Clippy (clippy.io), an AI video tool for small businesses, so I spend my days watching generated videos drift: labels melt, products change shape, and you can’t just move the logo in an MP4.

For this one I’m building PixiTween Director (startup track). A Muse Spark agent takes a product photo and a brief, draws the scenes with Muse Image and cuts the product and people into separate layers with SAM 3.1. It then animates them on our open-source PixiJS timeline, which plays live in the browser. It reviews its own frames, and you keep directing by chat (“bigger product in scene 2”). Real generated video only comes in when a shot needs it, and only after you approve the cost.

TypeScript, AWS and agent pipelines are my thing, and we already run Muse Spark and Muse Image in production. Happy to swap notes on SAM 3.1 or Muse Image consistency. Good luck everyone!

messages.author: Keith
messages.content:
Hey everyone, I'm Keith.

Solo builder in the Indie track, from Baton Rouge, Louisiana. I've spent 15+ years in infrastructure and security, mostly Linux and AWS, and right now I do IT at an Amazon fulfillment center, where I see hundreds of security alerts a day. Most of them are noise. The real ones get buried.

So I'm building True Positive, a triage assistant that pulls live GuardDuty and Security Hub findings, groups related alerts into incidents, scores them by real risk instead of raw severity, and drafts the fix, with a human approving every step. I'm also finishing a cybersecurity degree at WGU while I do all this.

This is my first hackathon. Happy to be here, and happy to swap notes with anyone building in security, AWS, or agentic workflows. Let's build something real this week.

messages.author: kali
messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋🇲🇽

I'm Alberto Castro, a software engineer from Mexico with experience in industrial automation, SCADA, backend development, and software architecture. I'm also studying Game Development Engineering.

I'm passionate about AI, local LLMs, and exploring unconventional approaches to software engineering.

For this hackathon, I'm building **CIDD — Contract Isolated Driven Development**.

**AI coding agents? I'm taking a different path. 😎**

CIDD is a contract-driven software generation engine powered by isolated LLM workers.

**No AI agents. No multi-agent orchestration. No repository access or tool execution for LLM workers.**

Instead, CIDD uses deterministic orchestration, isolated contracts, and local-first AI inference to generate software.

Our hypothesis: smaller local models can generate functional applications with significantly fewer tokens when the architecture handles the complexity.

**“The project grows. The worker's context doesn't.”**

We're building it from scratch during this hackathon. Let's see how far we can push this approach! 🚀

GitHub: https://github.com/itvboy/cidd

messages.author: CodeSphere PH
messages.content:
Hey everyone! 

I'm Kristoffer Aranas, a Full Stack Developer from the Philippines, and I'm building SMILE — See More of Iloilo’s Landmarks and Events, a gamified tourism and local commerce app designed to showcase the beauty, culture, food, festivals, and local businesses of Iloilo Province. 🇵🇭

The idea is to make exploring Iloilo more fun and rewarding! Visitors can discover landmarks, restaurants, festivals, and accommodations, check in using one-time QR postcards purchased from local merchants, collect digital stamps, and level up their travel status from Class E to Class SSS. 

I'm also exploring how Meta's Llama AI models can power SMILE Guide, a multilingual AI tour guide that creates personalized itineraries in English, Tagalog, and Hiligaynon. Other planned features include AI-assisted landmark photo verification, social media caption generation, product listing assistance for nano entrepreneurs, and tourism insights to help local government units make better-informed decisions.

I'm excited to explore how AI, tourism, and local commerce can work together to create opportunities for our communities, especially our local entrepreneurs and small businesses.

This is a project I'm passionate about, and I'm always open to feedback, suggestions, collaboration, and new ideas. If you're interested in tourism technology, AI, full-stack development, or community-driven innovation, I'd love to connect and learn from you!

🔗 GitHub: https://github.com/aranaskristoff2-ai

Good luck to everyone, and let's keep building something meaningful together!

messages.author: Drew Fortini
messages.content:
Hey everyone — Drew Fortini, Indie Dev Track, solo, Chicago. I'm an AI/ML architect and systems builder: I run a Proxmox/Ceph/Kubernetes homelab, build MCP tooling and agent infrastructure, and do MSP field engineering — which means I watch the same failure from both ends.

I'm building Handoff, a verification layer for procedural knowledge. Pipeline: first-person expert video (GoPro/webcam) → SAM 3.1 + Muse Spark decompose it into steps with tools, parts, preconditions, warnings → steps compile into a procedure graph → a checker mechanically flags missing steps, unmet preconditions, and out-of-order moves → the expert resolves each gap with one targeted question → trainees execute against the verified graph with live deviation detection.

The bar I'm holding myself to: ≥85% step recovery against hand-written keys across 5 real jobs, and 100% detection of deliberately removed steps.

The thesis underneath: agent harnesses are being wrapped around every layer of infrastructure, and they execute on human procedural knowledge that has never been verified. Harnesses aren't the bottleneck anymore — ground truth is. Handoff is the ground-truth layer.

Happy to compare notes with anyone on agent verification, video understanding, or human-in-the-loop systems — especially on how your harness decides something is "true."

LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/iamdrewfortini · GitHub: github.com/iamdrewfortini
Web: drewfortini.com · chromatixstudios.com · saucetech.io

messages.author: Johan Amezcua
messages.content:
Hello! 👋 I'm Johan, the creator of MolDesign, an app available on the Microsoft Store that aims to become an IDE for early-stage drug discovery.

For this hackathon, I'm building MolChat v2.0 on top of my existing MolDesign platform, transforming its chat assistant into an AI agent powered by Meta's models.

The goal is to let researchers use natural language or voice to run real computational chemistry workflows, draw and edit molecules in Ketcher 2D, generate videos visualizing their results, and export fully traceable run packages so other scientists can independently reproduce the work—all with human approval and verifiable scientific evidence.

messages.author: Trent Taylor
messages.content:
Hey everyone — Trent Taylor, checking in from Springville, Utah. By day I run dining services at a senior living community (chef/manager), and this is my first hackathon. Somewhere, my high-school guidance counselor is extremely confused right now. Solo builder, Indie track.

I'm building Intelligence Forge — a decision room for people who work alone. It's one chat app where a panel of AI models, with Muse Spark chairing, takes a hard decision from different sides, argues it out, and shows you exactly where they disagree instead of blending it all into one smooth answer. When you work alone, nobody stress-tests your thinking. This is the room that does. My day job is feeding a dining room full of seniors who are not shy with feedback, so a panel of AIs arguing with me just feels like a Tuesday.

Building on the Meta Model API, "Build for Your World" theme. Excited to see what everyone else is making — happy to trade feedback anytime.

messages.content:
👋 Hi all, I'm Adam, a solo full-stack developer from Nairobi, Kenya, in the Indie track. Really grateful to be part of this hackathon, and thanks to the organisers and Meta for putting it together!

I'm building Duka Books, a WhatsApp bookkeeper for Kenya's small shops ("dukas"). The owner sends a photo of their handwritten ledger, receipts, M-Pesa messages or a Swahili voice note. Muse Spark and SAM 3.1 turn those into proper books, and the owner confirms each entry with one tap. At month end they get a profit-and-loss statement they can take to a lender.

Stack: Convex, the WhatsApp Cloud API and the Meta Model API. By day I build BizStudio, a business app for Kenyan SMEs.

Happy to swap notes with anyone on WhatsApp bots, vision extraction from messy handwriting, or Swahili speech. I'd love to stay in touch after the hackathon too, so let's connect:

I'm trying to be honest about its limits too — it's front-only for now, and for graded cards it checks the slab cert alongside the card itself.

Happy to swap notes with anyone doing image or multi-signal checks.

messages.author: Waqar Javed
messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋 I'm Waqar Javed, an AI security researcher and founder of Safe Labs AI Inc., joining from the US as a solo builder in the Startup track.

I’m the creator of safelabs-eval, an open-source framework for red-teaming and evaluating text-based AI agents. For this hackathon, I’m building something new on top of that experience: Safelabs Guard — a runtime guard for multimodal agents.

Instead of only testing agents offline, Safelabs Guard verifies what an agent sees and hears before it acts. Using Muse Spark for reasoning, SAM 3.1 for visual verification, Muse Voice Transcribe for audio, and a deterministic step ledger, it can block an action when perception, voice instructions, and the task ledger don’t agree — including visual and audio prompt-injection attempts.

I’ll demo it on a small order-packing verification agent and measure guarded vs. unguarded performance across a set of reproducible multimodal attack scenarios.

Excited to Push the Frontier on multimodal agent security. I’d love to connect with others working on AI agents, evaluation, and agent safety — happy to exchange ideas and feedback! 🚀

Website: https://waqarjaved.com

Hi My name is Mayank Bhandari, I’m a Software Engineering Tech Lead with around 10 years of experience in software engineering, backend systems, distributed architecture, and building scalable applications.

For the Meta AI Hackathon, I’m building a **Multimodal Sign Language Kiosk** to break communication barriers between Deaf and hard-of-hearing people and the wider world.

The solution aims to use AI and computer vision to interpret sign language by analyzing hand gestures, facial expressions, and visual context, translating them into readable text and potentially spoken language. It will also explore converting spoken communication into accessible visual or sign-language responses to enable two-way interaction.

My vision is to make communication more inclusive and accessible worldwide, with potential applications in hospitals, airports, railway stations, government offices, educational institutions, and other public spaces. By leveraging Meta’s AI models and tools, I aim to turn this idea into a practical, scalable solution with meaningful global social impact.

messages.author: indranilpalit
messages.content:
Hi all, I’m Indranil, a senior SDET from Pune, India, in the Indie track. Grateful to be selected, and thanks to the organisers and Meta for running this.

I’m building ClipQuery, natural-language search over recorded camera footage. You ask “show me anyone who walked out carrying a box” and get the matching clips, marked on a timeline with the objects outlined — instead of scrubbing through six hours by hand.

I came to this from the other side. I built a PPE safety monitoring system on YOLOv8 and hit the usual wall: months of annotation, and it only ever saw the classes I trained it on. SAM 3.1’s open vocabulary removes that, so the interesting problem becomes relationships — “carrying” isn’t two masks overlapping, since a box sitting next to someone overlaps too. That layer is deterministic code on top of the model, which keeps results reproducible and explainable.

Stack: SAM 3.1 and Muse Spark 1.3 through the Meta Model API, Python, with the index stored locally so queries resolve in milliseconds. By day I’m the sole QA owner on a cloud governance platform in BFSI.

Happy to swap notes on open-vocabulary detection, multi-object tracking through occlusion, or anyone who’s fought spatial-relation logic before. Would like to stay in touch after the hackathon too — let’s connect:
Linkedin: www.linkedin.com/in/indranilpalit1996
Github: https://github.com/IndranilPalit24
X: https://x.com/IndranilPalit8

messages.author: Aditya Chawla
messages.content:
hi, I'm Aditya, a Full Stack AI Engineer from India 🇮🇳

I work on agentic AI systems, multi-agent orchestration, RAG pipelines, and real-time AI applications. I've also built [GuptAI](https://guptai.vercel.app/), a real-time multimodal AI desktop assistant.

For this hackathon, I'm building **CaseGraph AI** ⚖️

Recently, I spoke with a lawyer who told me how much time goes into processing 500+ page case files, researching judgments, and drafting legal documents. Even with tools like Claude, getting accurate, properly structured drafts takes multiple iterations and burns through a lot of tokens.

That got me thinking: **What if AI could understand an entire legal case instead of repeatedly reading the same documents?**

I'm planning to use Meta's models with agentic workflows, hybrid RAG, and knowledge graphs to extract facts, connect evidence, identify contradictions, research case law, and generate drafts with traceable citations, while keeping latency and token usage low.

Excited to experiment with Meta's models, learn from everyone here, and see what we all build!

Always happy to connect with fellow builders. Let's ship! 🚀

messages.author: Zoukmar
messages.content:
🧬 **Burotu: 50 cancers. One blood draw.**

Tumours leave tiny traces of their DNA in the blood. That DNA carries a methylation signature that hints at *whether* there's a cancer, and *where* it comes from.

This week I'm trying something a bit unusual: **teaching Meta's open-weight Muse Glimmer to read DNA methylation directly**, with a small adapter that turns a blood sample into tokens the model understands. The goal is a model that spots the cancer signal, points to the likely organ, and explains it in plain language.

First milestone done: a classic baseline to beat. On simulated plasma from held-out people, it catches 71% of cancers at 1% tumour DNA and nearly all of them at 3%, with 99.8% specificity. Now let's see if Muse can do better 👀

8 cancer types in the prototype, 50 on the roadmap, all on public TCGA + GEO data.
🌐 Live site: https://burotu.com
💻 Code: https://github.com/zoukmar/burotu

👋 I'm Michael, a software engineer from Paris 🇫🇷 (indie track). I've worked on a AI products over the years: LLM extraction, RAG, some computer vision etc…

If you know genomics, fine-tuning, or bio + AI, I'd love to swap notes. What are you all building? 🙌

Hello everyone, I am Shwe Win Aung, a freelance full-stack and trying to get into the FDE role  & I am from Mandalay, Myanmar,🇲🇲  currently pursuing an MCA in Delhi, India. I am participating solo in the Indie Developer track.

Project: Hsain Agent (working name), an AI back-office agent for small retail shops. The owner sends a voice note and a photo or short video of the shelf or a supplier invoice. The agent counts the stock, checks it against the ledger, flags discrepancies, drafts the supplier reorder, and sends it after the owner's approval.

Models: Muse Voice Transcribe (voice notes), SAM 3.1 (stock counting and segmentation), and Muse Spark 1.3 (invoice reading, reasoning, and tool-calling orchestration).

messages.author: Yuzuki Kondo
messages.content:
Hi everyone! 👋 I’m a climber and indie dev based in Japan.

What I’m building: a topo agent for bouldering gyms. You snap a photo of the wall and tap one hold. SAM 3.1 outlines every hold, then a Muse Spark agent picks out only the holds of the same problem, using tools to inspect, compare and zoom in. The result becomes a shareable problem in my climbing app. On my test walls it already beats my old color-based method, especially on tape-marked problems (14% → 100% recall).
Repo: https://github.com/Mirai-Climbing/topo-agent

Looking for teammates (up to 2 more): anyone into demo videos / social posts, mobile UI, or computer vision. Climbers very welcome! DM me 🙂

Questions:

How do we register as a team? Is it on the submission form or in the dashboard?
If people were accepted individually and then form a team, can the team submit only one project? Or can each member also submit their own solo project?

Hey everyone! 👋

I'm Ravindra, a 3rd-year student from Pune, India.

I'm passionate about building practical AI applications, working with structured data, and exploring how intelligent systems can solve real-world problems. Recently, I worked on a predictive analytics platform for public infrastructure monitoring, focusing on early risk alerts and explainable insights.

For this hackathon, I want to build towards ambitious frontier ideas—specifically prototyping one of these three concepts:

messages.author: rafatusa
messages.content:
Hey builders, I'm Rafat, founder of Royal Bengal AI. Staff platform / DevSecOps engineer by background, building AI products for South Asia.

Building Khet Saathi: an autonomous farm agent for the 100M+ smallholder farmers in India and Bangladesh, most of whom will never use a text-heavy app. The farmer just talks in Bangla or Hindi; the agent watches their land from space and runs the operation.

Live as of day zero, all on Meta models:
- SAM 3.1 segmenting individual farm plots from satellite imagery (39 fields in one frame, 1.4 s)
- Muse Voice Transcribe taking spoken Bangla, Muse Spark planning with tool calls and drafting seed/fertilizer orders, spoken reply back in Bangla
- Next: livestock (poultry shed) monitoring with SAM video tracking + Spark audio analysis, and an agent that phones buyers and negotiates the sale

Happy to talk satellite / geospatial pipelines, agent tool-calling or Indic voice. Always up for swapping notes.

messages.author: RudiZee
messages.content:
Hello everyone, I’m Rudi Coetzee.
Solo builder in the startup track, from George Town, Cayman Islands, originally from South Africa. I’ve spent 30+ years in IT (over 20 of those in cybersecurity leadership), mostly across GRC, threat modeling, cloud/K8s security, and web3/blockchain architectures. Right now I run Violet Sky Security SEZC as a fractional vCISO and DPO, where I see how easily real risk gets buried under noise, compliance checklists, multi-chain complexity, and agentic workflows that generate more alerts than signal.
So I’m building SPT-TXN, a privacy-preserving transaction authorization layer, threat triage for web3 and agentic systems that pulls live findings, groups related events into contextual incidents, scores them by actual risk rather than raw severity, and drafts the next step, with a human approving every action. I’m also advancing open-source work around SPT-Txn (TBAC + zero-knowledge privacy for multi-chain flows) and related IETF efforts while I do this.
Happy to be here, and happy to swap notes with anyone building in security, web3, zero-trust, or agentic workflows. Let’s build something real this week.
Https://foss.violetskysecurity.com
Https://github.com/rudizee007

messages.author: fabthenomad
messages.content:
Hey everyone — I'm Fabrice, founder of Outgrid. I live a digital nomad life, which is a bit different from just traveling, you know — you pick a place and you actually have to live there: the cost, the internet, the gym, how long you can legally stay, things like that.

Outgrid is the research I wished existed: 137 destinations scored for nomads, with real data on neighborhoods, coworking, costs, and stay rules. For this hackathon (Startup track, Build for Your World) I'm building the agent layer on top of it — a planner agent on Muse Spark that drafts a day-by-day plan from that data only, and a second agent on Muse Spark Open that checks every claim in the plan against the source records before anything reaches a traveler — no human in the loop, the second model is the gate. If a price or a visa rule isn't in our data, the plan doesn't get to invent it.

I'm building solo, and I'm building it from Bacalar, Mexico — one of the destinations in our own data, which is kind of the point. The research is firsthand because the life is firsthand. So it works out.

Happy to connect with anyone building agents that have to be *right*, not just fluent. Good luck to everyone.

Hey everyone! I’m Julie from Norway — I work offshore in the North Sea half the year, and build my own universe of projects the other half (YouTube channels, an AI short film, frequency music).

I’m building OTTERCEL GO 🦦 — an audio-first AI exploration game that gets people OFF their phones and out into the real world. One spoken mission at a time (“find something yellow”, “find a hidden entrance”), you explore eyes-up, tell the otter what you found, and it reacts with curiosity + XP. Running live on Muse Spark 1.3 already. First real field test today: the goal was a 5-minute walk in the rain — it became 18 minutes and a hidden stone cellar. 🕳️✨

Solo indie entrant, building with AI as my co-pilot. Background: 12 years running cinemas and leading teams, now a solo creator with 44K on TikTok — and I know firsthand what “I don’t feel like going outside” sounds like.

messages.author: Henry Mbugua
messages.content:
Hi @everyone! I'm Henry, a software engineer based in Nairobi, Kenya. I spent 5.6 years at Microsoft working on Microsoft Entra, and now I'm exploring what's next.

For this hackathon I'm building vexproof, an AI vulnerability analyst that answers one question: does this CVE actually reach my code?

Dependency scanners flag every vulnerable version. Most of those alerts never touch code your app calls, but someone still has to triage them by hand. vexproof uses Muse Spark to read advisories and fix commits, traces the call path into your code, and then deterministically verifies every claim before it outputs a verdict. The AI proposes. The verifier proves.

Day 1: I pointed it at an old Django project of mine. 96 advisory records turned into 94 real alerts (two were hidden duplicates). Next week's job is finding out how many of those 94 actually matter.

Happy to talk supply-chain security, Python tooling, or AI agents that have to be right. I'm also open to new roles, so if your team is hiring, let's chat.

GitHub: https://github.com/henrymbuguak
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/henrymbugua/

messages.author: VerbaGPT
messages.content:
Hi all, I'm Syed, a solo founder in Parker, Colorado. Background: healthcare actuary, 20 years in healthcare analytics and complex actuarial modeling.

My existing products (separate from my hackathon project):
- VerbaGPT (https://app.verbagpt.com/): A "talk to SQL" app, ask questions about your azure, snowflake, or even local SQL data in plain English; it writes the SQL or Python, runs it, and gives you charts and insights.
- MCPforX (https://www.mcpforx.com/): encode your professional expertise once as a markdown, a sequence or a decision tree, and run it from any AI tool.

For this hackathon I'm building Memex, an open-source (MIT) personal memory for any AI agent. Right now your context is fragmented across Claude, Codex and others. With Memex you point an agent at the repo ("hi agent, help me install this"), and it sets up your own Supabase and MCP server, costing pennies a month. Agents then sync what they know, even on a schedule, so you own your memory and aren't tied to any tool. Its (optional) "Dreaming" step runs on Meta's Muse Spark: it organizes and connects your memories and writes overviews of each topic. Repo going public soon. It builds on the excellent Open Brain project by Nate B. Jones.

I'd love to connect with people working on natural-language-to-SQL, agentic data analysis, local and private AI, the Meta Model API, and AI app security. Happy to swap feedback as we build.

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/smehmud

Looking forward to seeing what everyone makes! 🚀

messages.author: Wolv
messages.content:
Hey everyone! I’m Jan, based in the Netherlands, building solo in the Indie track.

For the hackathon I’m building TEMPO — a time-keeper agent for people who find time hard. If you’ve ever been reliably late not because you forgot the appointment but because “leave at 9:28” never turned into leaving at 9:28, this is for you — that’s time blindness, and it’s a daily struggle for a lot of people with ADHD and other neurodivergent folks, and plenty of neurotypical ones too.

TEMPO watches your calendar and your location, works out the real departure time, and nudges you at the moment it matters — not at a fixed offset. It learns the small stops you always make (coffee before morning meetings, groceries on Thursdays) so they’re built into the plan instead of being the reason you’re late. If you’re already late, it gives you one recovery action, not a list. You can tell it things by voice (“skip the coffee today”) or point the camera at an invite, poster or whatsapp message and it becomes an appointment. One number per screen, one tap per action — the design goal is zero cognitive load.

Under the hood, Muse Spark runs a tool-calling loop where deterministic tools compute every time and route and the model only decides and explains; Muse Voice Transcribe for voice, Spark vision for capture, Spark Open on Baseten as fallback. Every decision has a “why?” you can open from the notification. Stack: .NET 8 + React PWA.

Would love to hear from anyone building for executive-function support, or doing agents with hard guardrails. Repo: https://github.com/JanRaets/global-meta-ai-tempo·

messages.author: DaOriginalWombat
messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋 I'm Sisuthros, a Finnish builder based in Larnaca, Cyprus. Indie track.

By day, I work at a fintech company, handling payment and account escalations. I've seen what happens when a support bot promises something the actual policy doesn't allow.

That's why I'm building **Support Bot Rescue**: find where AI support agents break policy, fix the behavior, and prove the fix actually works.

My broader goal is to make AI agents safer and more reliable. I also work in AI model training and evaluation on the side, so yeah, you could say AI is my passion. 😁

**Day 1 results, using Meta models only:**
- A Muse Spark support bot for a fictional shop failed 6/15 test conversations.
- Muse Wonder rewrote its prompt. The first fix achieved zero policy violations.
- One small problem: it also denied a customer a completely legitimate $120 refund. 😂
- So we started testing both sides: what the agent must NEVER do, and what it MUST still do.
- The next version passed **15/15 tests + 5/5 sealed holdout cases** the fixer had never seen.

No LLM-as-judge. We use deterministic checks against actual tool calls, with reproducible results backed by a hashed manifest.

**Coming next:** A refund firewall where AI can propose actions but deterministic code makes the authorization decision, plus a Muse Wonder adversarial customer who absolutely refuses to take no for an answer.

And here's the slightly unusual part: I build with a family of five AI agents: **Lumen, Lumina, Prisma, Photon, and Aurora.** Each has their own role and personality. This week, they're directing Codex running on Muse Wonder. Expecting great things!

We're having fun, but the engineering is serious.

**If your agent can refund, cancel, or modify customer accounts, I'd love to swap failure cases.** 🔥

And if you'd like to collaborate, send me a DM!

GitHub: https://github.com/Sisuthros

messages.author: Mirkaso
messages.content:
👋 Hi everyone! I'm Kyrylo, a solo founder and developer from Spain.

https://www.linkedin.com/in/kyrylo-gaitan/

What I build
Mirkaso (mirkaso.com) is a crypto derivatives analytics platform: open interest, liquidations, funding, a signal scanner, sector indices and a macro regime view. I build the whole thing myself, from the FastAPI backend to the Next.js frontend. 

What I'm building here (Startup track)
Mirkaso Copilot is an agent on Meta Muse Spark that answers market questions through function calling over Mirkaso's market data.
The core idea is numeric grounding: the model never writes a number itself. Every figure in the answer is filled in by the server from tool results, so it can be traced to a source and a timestamp. There is also a guard that blocks financial advice, and a benchmark of Muse Spark against the model we run in production today.

Stack
Python (pydantic v2, httpx), FastAPI, Postgres, Redis, Next.js, Muse Spark via the OpenAI-compatible API.

Looking for
Feedback on grounding approaches for LLMs in finance, and other teams working on agents with tool use or on reliable numbers in LLM outputs.

Happy to chat, and the repo will be public soon. Good luck to everyone! 🚀

messages.author: matiasmolinas
messages.content:
👋 Hey everyone! I'm Matías, a solo dev from South America 🌎 — Indie track, *Build for Your World*.

🧠 **What I'm building: Athos** — your AI know-how, finally yours and portable.
I use coding agents for everyday work in any domain — tasks that along the way write code, run tools or control devices. Every time you teach an agent how *you* do something (your steps, your conventions, the mistakes to avoid), that knowledge gets stuck in one tool and one chat. Athos captures it as plain markdown on your machine and brings it to the next agent, so you never re-explain.

This week I got it working with **Muse Code on Muse Spark**: Claude Code learns a task once, Muse Code does the next one from a one-line request 🤯 It can also hand tasks you've already mastered to **Muse Spark through Meta Model API**, in Athos's own loop — about 5x cheaper than a frontier model on my test task. Little bars show how each agent does on *your* work, not someone else's benchmark.

🎬 23-second demo below 👇
⭐ Repo: https://github.com/athos-agent/athos

🙏 I'd love your help:
• **Try it** on a real task — one line to install, in Claude Code, Codex, or a plain terminal for Muse Code
• **Tell me what breaks** or what you wish it did → open an issue, bugs and feature ideas both very welcome
• If you like the idea, a **⭐ on GitHub** means a lot to a solo builder

And if you're fighting with Muse Code setup, ping me — happy to share what I learned 🙌

messages.author: markdeluca
messages.content:
Hey everyone!! I'm Mark DeLuca, from North Carolina. 👋

In my day job, I'm a Disaster Recovery Engineer. Off the clock, I'm the founder of The Find Me Project, a volunteer missing-person search team, and DeLuca Industries, where I build open-source tools to help solve community challenges.

My hackathon build is ARGUS, an AI review system of search teams' own drone imagery. Let's say a search team flies 3,000 drone photos. On average, nobody has the hours to review them all. ARGUS runs SAM 3.1 to segment candidates, Muse Spark to verify them against the case brief, and pins the ranked candidates on a search map for a human to verify. 

Day 1 and 2 are done and working. Ingest + tiling + map on my own drone photos, SAM found 4 candidates at 0.89-0.94 confidence, Muse honestly rejected the top one (0.1 — wrong jacket, right call). Next up, scaling the scan, a ranked review UI, and a benchmark that publishes a real recall score.

Solo builder, open source by default. Happy to trade feedback, and if you've done drone / SAR / mapping work, I'd love to compare notes.

messages.content:
Hi all, I'm Leo (github.com/dokutoshi), an ML research engineer on the indie track, based on US Eastern time. I've spent 20+ years moving from RF and edge hardware into ML, and I co-lead an LLM and RL study group for a data science meetup.

Building: a Dempster-Shafer+ belief-fusion RL agent. System 1 is deterministic fusion, and System 2 is an LLM reasoner that handles only the high-conflict cases. Conflict mass is a routing signal to use, not noise to normalize away. I'm testing dependability with order-invariance checks, seed variance, and cost versus an always-LLM baseline, all on synthetic data in a Gymnasium environment.

Looking for: feedback on reward design for process-level signals, and anyone working on agent reliability or reasoning under uncertainty. Happy to compare notes!

P.S. Two doctors, one patient... Dempster says tumor. 🙂

messages.author: Mohamed
messages.content:
Hi everyone! 👋

I'm an Assistant Professor at FSG, specializing in full-stack web and mobile development, with a strong focus on integrating LLMs into complex application architectures.

For this hackathon, I'm working on Socratix—an AI-powered educational assistant designed for university computer science labs. Instead of just generating code, it connects directly to students' local IDEs via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and uses Meta's API to guide them through Java OOP concepts using the Socratic method. Simultaneously, it streams real-time performance telemetry to a lecturer dashboard built with tools like Next.js and Supabase.

I'm really excited to dive deep into the Meta models for this EdTech architecture and push the boundaries of AI in education. Looking forward to seeing what everyone else is building and sharing ideas along the way! 🚀

messages.author: Mircea Rusu (Qubitpage.com)
messages.content:
Hello everyone, nice to meet you all! 👋
My name is Mircea Silviu Rusu
For the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Startup track) I'm building Carpathron: robots you can talk to, drive and become, powered by Meta's Muse models.

🧠 Muse Carpathron (Windows desktop app)
A full AI workspace for Windows 10, 11 and Windows Server 2016+, in the same league as Claude or ChatGPT desktop apps, built on Meta's models:
• Sign in with your Meta account (Muse Code) or use the Meta Model API (Muse Spark), with a model picker
• A real agent: files, PowerShell, web, MCP servers, parallel sub-agents, with Ask / Auto / Plan approval modes
• Memory that grows: RAG across all chats, Projects with knowledge files, auto-learned memories and skills
• Live activity view showing what runs locally on your PC and what goes to the cloud

📱 WhatsApp control (text + voice)
Link your WhatsApp and command everything from your phone, just like in the app. Send a voice note ("drive forward two seconds", "look left", "scan the room"): Muse Voice Transcribe turns it into an action, and photos and maps come straight back to the chat.

🚗 Baby Carpathron, the robot
An ESP32-CAM 4WD car with my own firmware: live video, RC-style driving, Wi-Fi setup, photos. The AI can drive it, "turn its head" to look around (the whole car turns, photographs and turns back), and scan a room. Muse Spark names what it sees and how far away, and builds a top-down map that's saved to memory.

🥽 Meta Quest 3S: avatar mode
• Carpathron Avatar, a native Quest app: the robot's camera fills your view, the controllers drive, and when you turn your head, the robot turns with you. Hold a grip and talk to Muse, or ask "what do you see?"
• Plus a browser VR mode and a passthrough AR mode straight from the Quest browser.

🔌 One open robot protocol
Every app speaks the same small open protocol, so any future robot that implements it works with the desktop app, WhatsApp, voice and the Quest app out of the box.

messages.author: Anna SD
messages.content:
Hey everyone! My name is Anna Soumayatou Diena I'm a software engineer from Senegal 🇸🇳
I'm excited to be part of this community and to explore what we can build with Meta's AI technology!
 I'm currently building Andado AI, a voice-first, multimodal AI assistant designed to empower blind and visually impaired people.
The idea is simple but meaningful: users should be able to take or upload a picture, ask questions about what they see, and receive clear, spoken descriptions of objects and their positions in the image. They should also be able to ask follow-up questions naturally.
My goal is to make AI more accessible, practical, and inclusive, especially for people who face visual accessibility challenges.
I'm currently developing the application and working on integrating Meta's AI API to bring its core features to life.
I'm passionate about software engineering, AI, accessibility, and building technology that solves real-world problems. I'm looking forward to learning from this community, sharing my progress, and connecting with other builders!
Let's build something meaningful together! 🌍💜

messages.content:
Hey everyone — I’m Sitesh Adhikari from Birtamode, Nepal 🇳🇵

I run Aahwan IT Group, and for the Meta Hackathon (Startup Track), I built Pizza Ghar — a production-ready, multilingual Voice AI ordering agent for a real restaurant client.

The Flow: A customer speaks in Nepali, English, or Hinglish. The AI extracts the order, updates the owner's live dashboard, generates a combined image of the meal, and sends a WhatsApp payment link.

The Stack:
🎙️ Ears: Groq Whisper (Nepali) + Meta Muse Voice Transcribe (Fallback)
🧠 Brain: Meta Muse Spark 1.3 via Model API (Strict JSON extraction)
🖼️ Eyes: Meta Muse Image 1.0 (Generates a combined photo of the cart)
⚙️ State: Node.js (Deterministic state machine to prevent hallucinations)

messages.author: Nuel
messages.content:
Hey all, Emmanuel here, building Vaultio on the startup track.

Vaultio is an assessment layer for technical hiring. The problem I keep running into: a CV tells you what someone claims, an interview tells you how well they talk, and neither tells you whether they can do the work.

For this build I'm going after the thing nobody has a test for yet. Engineers now work through agents, Claude Code and the rest, and that changes what "can they build" even means. So I'm building an assessment that captures how a candidate actually drives an agent: what they hand over, what they check, what they catch.

Part of the design is that the agent gets something wrong on purpose. The signal is whether the candidate notices. Candidates opt in for the assessment window and can revoke afterwards.

Two things I'd take from this group. If you hire engineers, or you've been through a hiring loop recently, tell me whether a record like that would have changed a decision you made. And if you want to try the assessment yourself, say so and I'll send it over.
https://vaultio.tech

Emmanuel

messages.author: MichælG_
messages.content:
Hey everyone! Michał here from Poland, building solo in the Indie Track. 🏎️💨

I'm building MetaECU Copilot - an autonomous, verifiable calibration engine for automotive ECUs (Bosch EDC16C39). 

Instead of guessing numbers like a generic chatbot, it reads real 2 MiB flash memory binaries, ingests 774 Bosch maps/curves, and runs a Deterministic Safety Gate enforcing physical mechanical boundaries (GM F40 transmission torque limits, Bosch CP1H Common Rail pressure caps, and bit-exact 32-bit checksum 0xD01FE500). If the model plans an unsafe torque (e.g. 450 Nm), the gate intercepts it and triggers an AI self-correction loop.

Track: Push the Frontier / Build for Your World
Stack: Meta Muse Spark, Muse Wonder, SAM 3.1 Vision, Python, WebGL 3D, Web Audio.

Includes an Interactive Web Cockpit, live WinOLS-style Binary Hex Diff, and standalone Windows desktop app (zero CMD!). 
Happy to connect with anyone working on verifiable agents, automotive tech, or embedded AI!

messages.author: Atabey Aydı
messages.content:
Hi builders! 👋

I’m Atabey, an electrical and electronics engineer who enjoys building at the intersection of AI engineering, embedded systems, electric machines, autonomous technologies, and industrial engineering.

My experience spans STM32 development, machine learning, computer vision, autonomous UAV systems, FPGA and Verilog HDL, PCB design, industrial analytics, and AI-based quality optimization. I’m especially interested in projects where software doesn’t remain isolated from the physical world but interacts directly with sensors, machines, control systems, and engineering processes.

What I’m building solo in the Indie track: An intelligent PMSM-oriented engineering platform that combines AI-assisted analysis, technical knowledge, motor-system data, and decision support. The broader vision is to investigate how generative and agentic AI can support engineers in understanding system behavior, evaluating technical evidence, and making better-informed engineering decisions.

Research scope: Like safety-critical automotive calibration systems, my platform follows a strict separation between probabilistic AI reasoning and deterministic physical verification. The agent may propose a Fuzzy-PID update, an RBFNN disturbance-compensation configuration, or a new simulation scenario, but MATLAB/Simulink evaluates the exact configuration against motor limits, controller bounds, model assumptions, and predefined benchmark rules. Unsafe, unstable, incomplete, or non-reproducible proposals are rejected before execution, and the rejection evidence is returned to the agent for constrained self-correction. Every accepted experiment is versioned and logged together with its parameters, model configuration, output signals, validation status, and performance metrics.

Excited to learn, experiment, and ship something impactful with this community! ⚡🚀

I’d be happy to connect with builders working on verifiable agents, electric drives, robotics, simulation automation, embedded co

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/nikolareljin

Project: Orphan Parts Lens

Most of us own more than we use, and the one part we need is usually the one that is missing. Orphan Parts Lens turns a drawer of idle hardware into a private inventory you can act on: scan what you own, find out whether a loose part or a Marketplace listing really fits, discover what your things could become, and prepare the rest for sale or free pickup. Built on Meta's Model API with Muse Spark, SAM 3.1 and Muse Voice Transcribe; the model proposes, the rules decide, and Marketplace stays yours. Web app, Android companion, one backend

messages.author: LSE Group
messages.content:
Hello everyone,

We’re pleased to share a special announcement for all teams working with GitLab in hosted or corporate environments.

Mnemosyne is our new product, built to meet the need for a central, team-wide AI documentation system. Instead of keeping development notes locally, Mnemosyne stores them on a server, organized per project and shared across every AI model your team uses. Teams can work on projects faster, and every model has access to the same central notes through SSO authentication and MCP access via Streamable HTTPS.

Our development team is spread across a dozen time zones, so we know the challenges of distributed work firsthand. Mnemosyne also addresses a growing concern for management: staying compliant without extra effort, and keeping disaster recovery and project documentation current at the push of a button, powered by AI.

Mnemosyne began as a standalone MCP project. During this Hackathon Challenge, we are extending it with a full web interface and SSO system. Together with MUSE AI and other AI interfaces, teams can create workflows, build Wikipedia-style documentation, and generate complete disaster recovery PDF documents at the click of a button.

Pending the executive decision at the end of November, the project will remain open source, so anyone who wants their own copy can fork it.

We wish all participants the best of luck.

https://github.com/lsegroup/mnemosyne

messages.content:
Update on Vee Vee — she's still free and live, and now her homework is public.

Her instruction core just passed an 89-question exam at 89/89 on Muse Wonder — then the identical, unchanged instructions passed 89/89 again on a second brain, Muse Spark 1.3. Same sheet, two brains, full marks both times.

The full record is in the repo as PROOF.md — including the failed first run, what she got wrong, and the exact fixes that earned the pass. I didn't hide the miss. She also got a design map (ARCHITECTURE.md) and a first screen that shows her systems with buttons to test them yourself.

Live: https://wayneherrington.github.io/veevee/
Repo: https://github.com/wayneherrington/veevee

Ask her something she can't know. She'll check — or she'll tell you she couldn't find it. That was the whole point of building her.

— Wayne (solo builder, first build of my life)

I’m working towards opening your desk and finding the important things already prioritised, with a first draft ready to work from. You review it and decide what goes ahead.

Would be good to meet others building around how people work day to day. What are you all working on?

messages.author: John
messages.content:
Hi all 👋 I'm Raj, founder of Lexcore Enterprises (India). We build and ship Android AI apps — a few are live on Google Play (Naira AI, Thali Calorie, Clay Music).

For this hackathon (Startup track, Build for Your World) I'm building SayLedger by Cortina: a voice + vision ledger agent for small shops. Speak an entry, snap an old handwritten ledger page, ask "how much credit is outstanding?" — Muse Voice Transcribe + Muse Spark + SAM 3.1, with all the maths done in code, never by the model.

Happy to swap feedback with other builders working on small-business or voice tools!

messages.author: Abheejit
messages.content:
Hola folks!

My intro - 

Abheejit is a social entrepreneur from Nagpur, India, with extensive experience across emerging technology, non-profit, and policy sectors. He is the Co-Founder of Social Innovation Labs, a global initiative HQ'd in Switzerland. He recently served as Digital Solutions Director at Catalyst Now, a global non profit network.

He has been recognized as a Top Innovator by the World Economic Forum, is an Amazon CTO Fellow, and Professional Fellow under US Department of State.

He founded  non-profit Vruksh Ecosystems, which focuses on grassroots entrepreneurship education and supports entrepreneurs across South Asia in their Zero to One journey. 

Abheejit regularly speaks at global conferences about his research and entrepreneurial work. He is passionate about using technology to create more equitable and accessible opportunities for all, and hopes to inspire others to follow their dreams and make a positive impact on the world.

abheejit.com - do connect 🙂
